chunks.heading: 2.2 Layout table (block origin BX = 320, BY = 138)
chunks.text: Total block extents: x 320 to 964 (with shadow), y 138 to 230. Fill area is the only place the HP is drawn.

chunks.heading: 2.3 Integration with the rest of the HUD
chunks.text:
- Wave banner: the banner is centred at y 240 and would collide with the readout and tab row (y 208 to 230). While the boss bar is shown, set the banner's y to 276 (glyph about y 231 to 321, clear of the bar, still above the usual fighting line of the far lane head height). One-line change in `HudScene` (`this.banner.setY(bossBar.visible ? 276 : 240)`), no other HUD element moves.
- LEVEL name text (y 100 to 124) stays. The plate starts 14 px below it.
- The small floating enemy bar over the boss is hidden while the boss bar is shown (section 10).

chunks.heading: 2.4 Several bosses
chunks.text: One full bar at a time. Rule: `slots = 2`. The first registered boss still alive gets the full bar. A second simultaneous boss gets a compact bar stacked 12 px below the full block: 640 x 24 frame (same layers, no plate row, name inline at the left in 18 px, no epithet, no skull tab, readout off, notch still drawn), at y = 242 (below the full block). When the primary dies its death sequence plays, then the secondary promotes to the full layout (slides up to y 138 and grows to full height over 220 ms Cubic.easeOut, instant under Reduced Motion). A third or later boss simply keeps its small floating bar. Level 1 wave 5 has only Dugan, so this is only exercised by future levels (bosses of the Level 3 and later fights are one at a time in the current content).

chunks.heading: 3. Data model
chunks.text: Per boss profile (`bossBar` JSON, section 12): `name`, `epithet`, `maxHp` (taken from the registered payload at runtime, the profile value is only a fallback), `rageThreshold` (0.30 for Dugan), optional `phaseNotches` (array of fractions, each drawn as an extra notch with no skull) and `palette` overrides. Profiles are keyed by the content id (`rust-brick-dugan`).

chunks.heading: 3. Data model
chunks.text:
Inputs at runtime:
- `entity-registered { id, team, boss: true, maxHp }`: start the intro and create a bar state. The payload has no name, so the HUD looks the profile up by `level.miniBoss` (levels.json has `"miniBoss": "rust-brick-dugan"` and `HudScene` already receives `this.level`). Adding an optional `profile` field to the payload later is additive and welcome; it is not required.
- `damage-applied { targetId, hpAfter, amount }` where `targetId` is a known boss: update `frac`, the drain chunk, the jolt and the rage crossing.
- `entity-died { id }` for a known boss: start the death sequence if the lethal `damage-applied` did not already.
- `retry` or scene shutdown: remove all bars at once (no animation).
- Per frame: `hp`, `maxHp`, `alive` from the shared state if the HUD polls; the event path above is enough and is the preferred source, so the bar can never disagree with the combat code.

chunks.heading: 3. Data model
chunks.text:
Pure rules (all in the data module, all unit testable):
- `frac = clamp(hp / maxHp, 0, 1)`.
- `raged = frac < rageThreshold` (strictly below, same as Dugan's `ragePending`: "below 30 percent"). Exactly 45 of 150 HP is not raged; 44 is.
- `critical = frac <= 0.10` (15 HP of 150).
- `band` = `rage` when raged, `critical` when critical (critical wins), else `high`.
- `displayFrac = min(introFrac, frac)`: a hit during the entrance never shows the fill above the real HP; the drain chunk starts only after the entrance finishes.

chunks.heading: 4. Fill, leading edge, tick marks
chunks.text:
Fill is flat: three horizontal bands inside the 584 x 20 trough, no gradients.
| Band | Body | Top highlight (6 px) | Bottom shade (4 px) | Extra |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| high (frac >= 0.30) | Visor Cyan #4FB3D9 | #A9DDF0 | #2F7FA3 | none |
| rage (0.10 to 0.30) | Hazard Orange #F58A2A | #FFB36B | #B85F14 | diagonal ink hatch on the fill (section 5.3) |
| critical (<= 0.10) | Enemy Critical #C9452F (NOT Telegraph Red #FF3B30) | #E9715C | #8E2F20 | hatch plus sawtooth leading edge (section 8) |
Band changes are hard steps except at the rage crossing (section 6). Rage Orange #F58A2A is the existing "Rage Orange / Ember" value; it is shared with Zed's Rage meter, but this bar is the Rust-frame, top-centre, hatched one, so the shape language differs (style guide 10.5: tie every colour change to a shape or text change, which section 11 does).

chunks.heading: 4. Fill, leading edge, tick marks
chunks.text:
Leading edge: a 3 px vertical strip at the fill's right end, full 20 px height, colour Spark Cream #FFF6D6 alpha 0.9 (the one bright element of the bar, it reads as the live HP). When a hit lands the edge widens to 10 px and fades back to 3 px over 120 ms (Quad.easeOut) (section 6.4 for flash safety). The edge is clipped to the fill: at frac 0 it is not drawn.
Tick marks every 25 percent: at 25, 50 and 75 percent (x = 494.0, 640.0, 786.0). Each is a 2 px wide Rust Ink #14181C line at alpha 0.55, 6 px long from the top edge of the trough (y 178 to 184) and 6 px from the bottom (y 192 to 198), drawn over the fill, plus a 1 px Steel Light #A9B6C1 line at alpha 0.5 at the same x on the steel band above (y 172 to 175) so the tick reads from the frame as well. They are 25 percent of max HP, so for a 150 HP boss the ticks sit at 37.5 HP steps.
Trough background: Gunmetal #2A3138 with a 1 px Rust Ink line at the top (inner shadow). Inside the danger zone the trough has the brick-red hatch (below).

chunks.heading: 5.1 Notch
chunks.text: A vertical Rust Ink 3 px line at x = 523.2 over the full block height from y 170 to 206 (through both steel bands), crossing the fill. A 1 px Steel Light highlight 1 px to its left. Always visible, both before and after the crossing, so the player can see the line and how far the boss is from it from the first second.

chunks.heading: 5.2 Danger zone (x 348 to 523.2, 0 to 30 percent)
chunks.text: The zone is drawn in the trough background, behind the fill, so it is visible as soon as the fill (and the cream chunk) drains out of the 0 to 30 percent segment, and is hidden behind the fill while the boss is healthy. Brick Dark #5A1F18 base at alpha 0.85 with 45 degree Rust Ink hatch lines at alpha 0.5 (2 px wide, 8 px pitch, clipped to the zone). The hatch is the signal, brick red is secondary; the left cap's hazard stripes point the same way. Before rage the fill sits over it, so the zone is shown ahead of time by the notch line and skull tab (5.1, 5.4); the hatch itself shows through when the fill drops below 30 percent.

chunks.heading: 5.3 Hatch on the fill
chunks.text: When the band is rage or critical the fill gets the same 45 degree Rust Ink hatch at alpha 0.18, 8 px pitch, so a colour-blind player gets a pattern change as well as an orange change. In Full motion the hatch scrolls left at 20 px/s while raged (static under Reduced Motion).

chunks.heading: 5.4 Skull tab and glyph
chunks.text:
Steel tab under the frame, (511, 208, 24, 18), 2 px Rust Ink outline, 2 px bevel (Steel Light top and left). Skull glyph centred at (523, 217), primitives only, 14 px wide: cranium circle r 5.5 Cream #F4E6C8, jaw rect 7 x 3 under it, two eye holes (2.5 px circles) and a nose notch in Rust Ink. A small 8 px copy of the skull sits inside the ENRAGED tag.
- Before the crossing: glyph Cream on a Steel tab ("a warning on the wall").
- After the crossing: the tab turns Hazard Orange #F58A2A, the skull turns Rust Ink with Cream eye holes, and a three-tongue flame crown (triangles, 6 px high, Hazard Orange with a #FFD24A inner tongue) burns above the skull behind the tab (flicker 3 Hz, tongue heights jitter +/-2 px, static under Reduced Motion).

chunks.heading: 6. Timeline and motion
chunks.text: All times are real time ms (HUD clock). Easing names are Phaser tween names.

chunks.heading: 6.1 Entrance (from `entity-registered { boss: true }`)
chunks.text: Starts `introDelayMs` 400 after registration so the wave banner and Dugan's walk-in are not stepped on. Total about 1200 ms of motion after that. The bar does not block input or gameplay.

chunks.heading: 6.1 Entrance (from `entity-registered { boss: true }`)
chunks.text:
| t (ms) | What happens |
|---|---|
| 0 | Frame appears as an iris wipe from the centre: visible half-width 0 to 320 px over 260 ms (Cubic.easeOut). Trough empty, no fill, no notch tab yet. Shadow wipes with it |
| 200 | Name text starts, scale 2.4 to 1.0 over 140 ms (Cubic.easeIn), alpha 0 to 1 over the first 60 ms. The plate fades in under it over 120 ms |
| 340 | SLAM impact (name reaches scale 1): plate and name jolt 4 px down and settle over 100 ms (Quad.easeOut); 8 dust rects (Steel and Slate, 3 to 5 px, speed 90 to 220 up-and-out, gravity 700, life 260 to 380) from the plate's bottom edge; camera shake call-out on the arena camera: 160 ms, intensity 0.004 (about 5 px, same as the KO shake); screen-edge pulse (section 6.6) |
| 300 to 1200 | Fill grows from 0 to `frac` over 900 ms (Cubic.easeOut: fast start, slow finish). The leading edge strip rides the fill front. Each time the front passes a tick (25, 50, 75) the tick brightens to Steel Light for 80 ms (a small "latch" cue, no white). Notch tab and skull fade in at t 700 over 200 ms |
| 500 | Epithet slides in from +16 px to its place and fades in over 200 ms (Cubic.easeOut), after the name has landed |
| 1000 | HP readout fades in over 150 ms |
| 1200 | Entrance done. Drain and hit reactions are fully live (they work from t 0 on `displayFrac` but a hit during the entrance only clamps the fill and skips the chunk) |

chunks.heading: 6.1 Entrance (from `entity-registered { boss: true }`)
chunks.text: Camera shake and the edge pulse are the optional call-outs. They are in the data so the owner can turn either off (`intro.cameraShake`, `intro.edgePulse`).

chunks.heading: 6.2 Damage chunk (the trailing "ghost")
chunks.text:
Same as the enemy bar but tuned for a 584 px bar (hit-feedback-spec 7.1 uses hold 300 / shrink 250 on a 90 px bar; a boss hit is a bigger visible loss, so hold is a bit longer):
- Cream #F4E6C8 segment from the new fill front to the previous displayed edge (`drainFrom`), alpha 1.
- Hold 350 ms, then shrinks to the new front over 300 ms (Quad.easeOut, `easeOutQuad`).
- A hit during the hold keeps the older left edge (`drainFrom`), exactly as `barOnDamage` in `hitFeedbackData.js`; a hit during the shrink starts from the currently shown edge. Same maths, so the two bars feel the same.
- Chunk debris (Full motion only): when the chunk starts shrinking, spawn `min(6, ceil(dropFrac x 40))` tiny rects 3 x 3 px Cream and Steel from the chunk's left end, falling (gravity 900, small outward vx 20 to 70, life 280 to 360, alpha out over the last 40 percent), at most 14 alive.
- Lethal hit: no hold (chunk shrink starts immediately, 250 ms) as in the enemy bar KO rule.

chunks.heading: 6.3 Hit reaction (every `damage-applied`, amount > 0)
chunks.text:
- Jolt: the frame group (frame, fill, hatch, caps, tab) drops 3 px on a light hit (amount < 12, the same `heavyAt` 12 as `EnemyHitFx`) and 5 px on a heavy or finisher hit, then returns over 110 ms (Quad.easeOut). The plate and name follow at 50 percent (1.5 px and 2.5 px). Rate limit: a new jolt may start only 60 ms after the previous one started (chunk and fill still update every hit). No horizontal shake on a plain hit.
- Leading-edge flare: edge widens to 10 px, 120 ms (above).
- Fill flash: the last 40 px of the fill (the region just behind the edge) tints to Spark Cream #FFF6D6 alpha 0.9 for 66 ms (light), 83 ms (heavy, finisher, ko). Only 40 px of a 584 px bar flashes, so the bright area is about 800 square px, far under the "no large flashes" guidance; and only if 120 ms have passed since the last fill flash (`flashRateLimitMs`). A combo only brightens every other hit.
- No colour change of the whole frame on a plain hit.

chunks.heading: 6.4 Flash and strobe safety
chunks.text: Total bright events from this bar: edge flash at most 8 per second (120 ms limiter), the rage crossing flash once, the entrance edge pulse once, the death burst once. The rage and critical pulses are slow, soft amplitude changes of orange and not white (below). Nothing exceeds 3 per second at full contrast.

chunks.heading: 6.5 Phase change: crossing below the rage threshold
chunks.text: Fires once, on the first `damage-applied` where `raged` becomes true (`frac < rageThreshold` and the bar was not raged). Also fires on a retry spawn only if the new boss starts raged (it does not).

chunks.heading: 6.5 Phase change: crossing below the rage threshold
chunks.text:
| t (ms) | What happens |
|---|---|
| 0 | The hit's normal jolt (use heavy size, 5 px) and chunk. Frame flash: the steel bands and notch line flash Spark Cream #FFF6D6 at alpha 0.85 for 80 ms, decaying to 0 over the next 160 ms (Quad.easeOut). Skull tab pops: scale 1 to 1.6 to 1 over 240 ms (Back.easeOut), the skull ignites (section 5.4). Fill band swaps to rage. Fill colour crossfades from cyan to Hazard Orange over 200 ms (linear, not through white) |
| 0 | Camera shake call-out on the arena camera: 200 ms, intensity 0.004 (about 5 px). Screen-edge pulse in Hazard Orange (section 6.6), stronger than the entrance one (peak alpha 0.30) |
| 0 to 400 | Name plate shake: x offset +/-3 px alternating every 40 ms (25 Hz, 10 half-cycles), amplitude decays linearly to 0 by 400 ms. The plate border turns Hazard Orange and the plate fill Brick Dark #5A1F18 (hard step at t 0, stays) |
| 100 | "ENRAGED" tag slams in right of the plate: scale 1.8 to 1.0 over 120 ms (Cubic.easeIn) and a 3 px jolt of its own |
| 0 to 260 | Heat sweep: an Hazard Orange hatch band (the danger zone hatch) sweeps in from the notch to the left cap (x 523 to 348) over 260 ms (Cubic.easeOut), after which the zone hatch stays brighter (alpha 0.5 to 0.75) |
| 0 on | Sustained rage state (section 6.7) |

chunks.heading: 6.6 Screen-edge pulse (call-out)
chunks.text: HUD scene graphics layer, four frames of 28 px along the screen edges built from 4 stacked 7 px strips at alpha 0.45, 0.30, 0.18, 0.08 of the peak (stepped, no gradient). Colour Hazard Orange #F58A2A. Entrance: peak alpha 0.18, up in 60 ms, down over 300 ms (Quad.easeOut). Rage crossing: peak alpha 0.30, up in 60 ms, down over 400 ms. It sits under the bar and under every HUD text, never covers the lane centre (28 px at the edges only). Death burst uses Gold #FFD24A at peak 0.15, 250 ms.

chunks.heading: 6.7 Sustained rage pulse (while `raged`)
chunks.text:
- Heat halo: three nested 1 px rect strokes around the frame, offsets 4, 8 and 12 px, Hazard Orange, base alphas 0.50, 0.30, 0.15, multiplied by pulse(t) = 0.5 + 0.5 x sin-wave, 1.6 Hz (period 625 ms), range 0.30 to 1.0 of base (Sine.easeInOut feel).
- Fill top highlight: pulses between #FFB36B and #FFD9A8 at the same 1.6 Hz.
- Skull flame flickers at 3 Hz (small and local).
- Danger-zone hatch scrolls left at 20 px/s.
- Plate border pulses Hazard Orange to #FFB36B at 1.6 Hz.
Everything is slow and small amplitude (max alpha swing about 0.35), under the 3 Hz flash limit.

chunks.heading: 6.8 Low HP danger state (frac <= 0.10, bar `critical`)
chunks.text:
Shape, text and rate all change, not only colour:
- Fill body Enemy Critical #C9452F with the hatch of rage kept.
- Leading edge becomes a sawtooth: 3 teeth, each 4 px wide and 6 px deep, in Spark Cream, instead of the straight 3 px strip (shape cue).
- Pulse rate rises from 1.6 Hz to 2.5 Hz (halo and fill top). Never above 2.5.
- The readout turns Hazard Orange #F58A2A and gets a trailing "!" ("12/150 !"): a text cue.
- The tick and notch are unchanged.
Entering critical does not repeat the rage crossing effects; a single 3 px jolt only.

chunks.heading: 6.9 Death / defeat (about 700 ms)
chunks.text: Starts on the lethal `damage-applied` (`hpAfter <= 0`), or on `entity-died` if no lethal damage event was seen. Dugan's own KO fall (hit-feedback-spec: KO falls over 400 ms, hit-stop and shake belong to combat) plays in the arena at the same time; the bar matches that KO feel: sharp, then it leaves.

chunks.heading: 6.9 Death / defeat (about 700 ms)
chunks.text:
| t (ms) | What happens |
|---|---|
| 0 | Lethal-hit jolt (5 px) and edge flare as usual. Drain chunk starts shrinking immediately (no hold), 250 ms (Quad.easeOut) to empty. Halo, hatch scroll and plate shake stop, pulse freezes at 0.5 |
| 0 | Camera shake call-out: 150 ms, 0.004 (the existing KO number, 5 px). No edge pulse from the bar here (the combat code owns the KO flash); only a Gold pulse of 0.15 peak at t 250 |
| 250 | The empty frame SHATTERS: 12 pieces (10 equal slices of the 584 px middle body, 58.4 px wide, plus the two caps). Each piece is a rect with the same layers (ink outline, steel band, trough). Order outward from the centre: delay = |i - 4.5| x 14 ms (0 to 63 ms). Motion: initial hop vy -120 px/s, gravity 1800, vx = (i - 4.5) x 18 px/s, rotation to +/-(8 to 24) degrees depending on side (they are shards, not HUD text), life 380 ms, alpha 1 to 0 over the last 40 percent. Slices are hidden behind nothing (they fall over the lane edge; they may overlap the lane, they are only 380 ms and alpha-fading) |
| 250 | Burn-down: 16 sparks from random x along the frame top, rect 6 x 2 px, cone 80 to 100 degrees up +/-40, speed 120 to 320, gravity 600, life 300 to 500, colours by life: Gold #FFD24A, Hazard Orange #F58A2A, Rust brown #9C5A2E (no White stop, so no flash). 6 smoke puffs (Slate #3C4650, size 14 to 24, rise 20 px, alpha 0.5 to 0, life 400) |
| 300 to 600 | Name plate, ENRAGED tag, epithet, readout fade out over 300 ms (alpha 1 to 0, Quad.easeIn) while they sink 10 px (no rotation). Epithet and readout fade first (250 to 400) |
| 700 | Everything destroyed, bar slot freed (and a secondary boss, if any, promotes) |

chunks.heading: 6.9 Death / defeat (about 700 ms)
chunks.text: Reduced Motion version: drain 250 ms as normal, hold the empty frame 100 ms, then the whole block alpha 1 to 0 linearly over 350 ms (350 to 700), no slices, no sparks, no smoke, no shake.

chunks.heading: 7. Layering
chunks.text:
`HudScene` sits above `ArenaScene`. Depths inside `HudScene` (the existing HUD objects use default depth 0 to 9; the Rage meter uses 6 to 9):
| Depth | Object |
|---|---|
| 20 | Screen-edge pulse graphics |
| 21 | Shadow, trough, danger zone, skull tab (frame back layer) |
| 22 | Fill, chunk, hatch, ticks, notch, leading edge |
| 23 | Frame bands, caps, rivets, halo strokes |
| 24 | Name plate, ENRAGED tag |
| 25 | Text: name, epithet, readout |
| 26 | Debris, shards, sparks, smoke (death and entrance) |
Three Graphics objects (`back`, `fill`, `front`), one more for particles, plus Text objects for name, epithet, tag and readout. All cleared and redrawn each frame (like `EnemyHitFx.update`). Pause: `BossBarHud.update(time, delta)` is driven from `HudScene.update` and clamps `delta` to 50 ms, so animations freeze with the scene and cannot jump when resumed.

chunks.heading: 8. Text and font notes
chunks.text:
- Name: `FONTS.button` (Anton) because the heavy condensed face is the industrial one; `FONTS.display` (Permanent Marker) is the Hope hand-drawn font and is kept off Rust UI on purpose.
- All text waits for `waitForFonts()` (already done before scenes start); first draw happens after fonts load.
- Contrast: Cream on Rust Ink about 13:1; Steel Light #A9B6C1 on Rust Ink about 8.6:1 (epithet); Rust Ink on Hazard Orange about 7:1 (tag); readout Cream on stroke 4 px.
- Name content: "BRICK DUGAN" (the content name is `"Brick" Dugan`; the plate drops the quotes and uppercases). Epithet (proposed): "THE HUMAN BATTERING RAM", taken from the GDD tone in `mini-bosses.json` ("built like a human battering ram"). It is a descriptive tag, not new lore: he stays a former dock worker recruited into the Rust and no rank or title is invented. Alternative that is strictly canon: "FORMER DOCK WORKER". Open question 1.

chunks.heading: 9. Readout decision
chunks.text: Show a small numeric readout ("98/150") under the bar at the right. Reasons: Dugan has 150 HP and the player's own bar already shows numbers in the same format, so it costs no new reading rule; with chunky 3.9 px per HP the exact number helps the first learning attempts and the playtest. It is small, off the bar (not on the fill), and a data flag (`readout: 'none'`) removes it for polished bosses. Default `hp`.

chunks.heading: 10. Integration notes (not changing gameplay)
chunks.text:
1. Hide the small floating bar over a boss with a big bar. `EnemyHitFx.onDamage` creates a `bars` entry for any enemy that takes damage. Add an optional constructor option `hasBossBar(id)` (or a shared `bossBarIds` Set exported from `bossBarData.js`) and skip bar creation and drawing for those ids. Because the boss bar creation (entity-registered) happens before the first damage, the floating bar never shows for Dugan. Reset on retry.
2. `telegraphBottomY(id)` returns `null` when an enemy has no small bar. Dugan's telegraph icons (Brick Breaker Punch, charge strip, stomp circle, the grab cue) must fall back to the sprite-top position in that case. Check this in the Dugan code path; if the telegraph icon anchors to the bar top, return the same y the small bar would have used for Dugan (`barPosition(...)`-derived) without drawing it.
3. Camera shake call-outs run on the `ArenaScene` main camera (`this.scene.get('ArenaScene').cameras.main.shake(ms, intensity)`), scaled by the Options screen shake scale: `st.reducedMotion === true ? 0 : shakeScale(st.screenShake)` (the same helper `MegaStompFx` and `WallSlamFx` use). The HUD itself is not shaken.
4. Settings read: `loadSettings(globalThis.localStorage)` in try/catch; `reducedMotion`, `screenShake` and `hitFlash` ('Low' | 'Medium' | 'High') as in `optionsData.js`. Re-read at each trigger so Options changes apply immediately.
5. Banner y shift (section 2.3).
6. Level-start order: the bar's intro starts 400 ms after `entity-registered`; if the boss is registered before `HudScene` exists (the HUD scene is created after the arena), seed from `ArenaScene` state in `create()` the same way `RageMeterHud` seeds from the level number.

chunks.heading: 11. Accessibility
chunks.text:
Reduced Motion (Options `reducedMotion`):
- No wipe, no name slam, no slide: the whole block fades in over 200 ms and the fill appears full at that moment (instant fill; the leading edge is still drawn).
- No camera shake, no plate shake, no jolt, no dust, no sparks, no shards, no debris, no flame flicker, no hatch scroll.
- Pulse becomes a static look: halo fixed at 0.30 of its range (alpha 0.15, 0.09, 0.045), fill top highlight fixed, critical state static.
- The drain chunk still shows and shrinks (it is information, not decoration); entrance edge pulse and rage edge pulse become a static 150 ms fade of peak alpha 0.10.
- Death: section 6.9 fade.
Hit Flash Low (Options `hitFlash === 'Low'`, independent of motion):
- No Spark Cream or White flash anywhere. Fill flash tint becomes #BFC8CF (`REDUCE_FLASH_TINT`), leading-edge colour stays Spark Cream at alpha 0.6 instead of 0.9 (no flash, a static edge), frame flash at the rage crossing becomes Sand #E8C27A alpha 0.45 for 160 ms, screen-edge pulse peak alpha 0.12 (entrance 0.08), death sparks start at Gold (they already do), edge flash limiter 240 ms.
- Shake and zoom are not flashes and follow their own settings.
Colour is never the only signal:
- Rage state: ENRAGED text tag, skull ignition and flame crown, plate shake, hatch pattern on the fill, notch always present, pulse (when motion allowed).
- Low HP: sawtooth leading edge, readout colour plus "!" text, faster pulse.
- Healthy vs damaged: cyan fill versus empty trough, with length as the main signal, plus the numeric readout and ticks.
- Danger zone: hatch and notch line, not just red.
- Chunk vs fill: cream chunk is also a different position/length.
- Cyan vs orange fill under deuteranopia: the two differ in lightness (cyan #4FB3D9 is lighter) and in the hatch overlay.

chunks.heading: 12. Machine-readable data (`bossBar`)
chunks.text: Every number is px or ms; colours are hex strings (convert with `hex()` in the data module like `hitFeedbackData.js`); `ease` values are Phaser tween ease names. Profiles are keyed by content id. Copy straight into `src/ui/bossBarData.js` as `BOSS_BAR` and `BOSS_PROFILES`.

chunks.heading: 12. Machine-readable data (`bossBar`)
13. Suggested test coverage (`bossBarData.test.mjs`)
chunks.text: Pure maths worth pinning: `fillArea` (584 x 20) and `notchX(0.30)` = 523.2; `tickXs()` = 494, 640, 786; `isRaged(0.30)` false, `isRaged(44/150)` true; `bandFor(frac)`; `displayFrac` clamps to `min(introFrac, frac)`; drain hold and shrink behave like `barOnDamage` (hit during hold keeps `drainFrom`; lethal skips the hold); `joltAmplitude(amount)` 3 or 5 and the 60 ms rate limit; flash limiter 120 ms (240 under Hit Flash Low); `pulse(t, hz)` range and `maxPulseHz` clamp (never above 2.5); `introFill(t)` at t 300 (0), 750 (about 0.875 of the eased value), 1200 (1); `shatterPieces()` count 12 and delays 0 to 63 ms; `clipPolygonToRect` for the hazard stripes; Reduced Motion and Hit Flash Low resolution tables returning the values above; stacking (`slots`, promotion order, a third boss gets no big bar); profile lookup fallback via `level.miniBoss`.

chunks.heading: 14. Asset and manifest note
chunks.text: No image assets. Everything is Graphics rects, polygons, circles and Text. The skull and flame are polygons and circles. Nothing here is final art; it is a code-drawn placeholder-quality spec that can be skinned later with a 640 x 40 frame sprite without changing the data (the fill area rect is the contract).

chunks.heading: Dugan Grab Break prompt (art and feedback spec)
chunks.text: Status: PROPOSED starting values for playtest. Owner: art-direction-agent. Covers the bubble shown above Zed while "Brick" Dugan holds him (Grab and Wall Slam, and the running-grab catch). Feedback only: the break rule (6 taps of Light J/Z, Heavy K/X or jump Space fill the meter, `breakTaps` = 6, Dugan stunned 0.8 s), `holdMs` = 900, 22 damage and the Wall Slam impact are fixed inputs and are not changed here. Primitives only (Phaser Graphics plus two pooled Text objects), no new assets. Pixel-art flavour: chunky outlines, integer pixel positions, flat fills, no gradients, no blur, no glow. Times are ms from the start of the hold (`zed.grab.timer` = 0). Slam = `holdMs`.

chunks.heading: 1. Intent
chunks.text:
The player has under one second and must read three facts without reading words: (1) press THIS button, (2) press it a lot, (3) there is a clock. One round bubble does it:
- A big orange key cap in the middle shows the button and visibly "presses" at a fast mash rhythm (the verb).
- An outer ring is the clock. It DRAINS to empty at exactly the slam frame.
- Six pips under the key cap are the progress. They FILL, one per tap.
How the two meters never get confused: they are different shapes, different colours and move in opposite directions. The outer ring is a thick cream band that shrinks (goes away = danger coming, turns red at the end). The pips are green blocks that grow (coming in = good). Rule for the player: "fill the green before the ring runs out". Neither meter uses the other's colour, and each is readable in grey-scale by shape alone (a shrinking circle against a row of boxes filling up). The key cap carries the orange accent so the eye lands on the verb first, then the ring, then the pips.

chunks.heading: 1. Intent
chunks.text: The cue is driven by the real simulation, not tweens: ring = `1 - timer / holdMs` each frame (so it is empty on the very frame the slam fires, whatever `holdMs` is), pips = `zed.grab.progress * breakTaps`.

chunks.heading: 2. Anatomy (bubble local coordinates, centre = 0,0, +y down)
chunks.text:
| Part | Spec |
|---|---|
| Outline disc | radius 55, Dark Brown #2E1F16 (this is the 3 px outer outline) |
| Timer track | the dark band from radius 46 to 52 (shows through where the ring has drained) |
| Timer ring | arc stroke 6 px centred at radius 49, starts at 12 o'clock, drains from its end (see 3.2), butt caps, colour by state |
| Separator | 3 px Dark Brown between ring and body (radius 43 to 46) |
| Body | cream disc radius 43, Spark Cream #FFF6D6 |
| Key cap | 36 x 36 at (0, -8), Orange #F58A2A fill, 3 px Dark Brown outline, 4 px darker "side" under it #B85F14 (the cap depth), label Dark Brown (contrast about 6:1 on the orange) |
| Pips | 6 squares, 8 x 8 including a 2 px Dark Brown outline, gap 2, row centred at (0, +24), total width 58 (fits the body chord, 65 px at that height) |
| Tail | triangle, base 18 px on the ring edge, length 16 px (min 10, max 22), Dark Brown 3 px outline, cream fill, points at Zed's head. Drawn under the disc so the disc hides the tail base |
| Hint pill (first time only) | 64 x 24 pill at (0, -69), Orange fill, 3 px Dark Brown outline, text "MASH!" |

chunks.heading: 2. Anatomy (bubble local coordinates, centre = 0,0, +y down)
chunks.text: Overall footprint: 110 px bubble (+16 px tail), small against the 192 px Dugan and 1280 x 720 view, big enough to read in a glance.

chunks.heading: 2.1 Key label (variable, never hard-coded)
chunks.text:
The label text is `keyLabel(KEY_MAP.light[0])` from `src/player/input.js`, so a rebind changes it. Layout function: strip `Key` and `Digit`, `Space` becomes `SPACE`, `ArrowUp/Down/Left/Right` become the glyph words `UP DOWN LEFT RIGHT`, `ShiftLeft` becomes `SHIFT`, everything else upper-cased. The cap grows to fit: cap width = clamp(textWidth + 18, 36, 64); the height stays 36. Font size by length: 1 char 28 px, 2 to 3 chars 20 px, 4 to 5 chars 16 px. Font: the game's button face, `FONTS.button` (Anton, fallback Impact) from `src/config/assetKeys.js`; Anton at 28 px reads as a solid block letter at this size. Re-read the label every time the cue is shown (a bind can change between grabs), not once at boot.
Which button is shown: the Light attack (default J). The cue accepts any attack or jump, but showing three keys would not read in a glance. A small `Z` or `SPACE` secondary is NOT shown (see open question 3). Heavy is not shown even though it works, because the one best-known verb is the clearest.

chunks.heading: 2.2 Gamepad variant
chunks.text: If a pad is the last-used input device, the cap becomes a circle (radius 19, same colours) labelled with the face button for `PAD_MAP.light` (index 2): Xbox-style and unknown pads show `X`; PlayStation-style pads (id contains DualShock, DualSense or Wireless Controller) draw a square outline primitive (14 x 14, 3 px) instead of text; Nintendo-style pads show `Y` (standard mapping index 2 is the left face button, which is labelled Y there). The label comes from `PAD_MAP.light[0]` so a pad rebind follows. The last-used device is whichever of keyboard or pad produced the last input.

chunks.heading: 3. States and timing
chunks.text: Let `t = timer / holdMs` (0..1), `timeLeft = holdMs - timer`, `urgencyMs` = 250.

chunks.heading: 3.1 Pop-in (0 to 80 ms)
chunks.text: First draw is on the same frame the state becomes `held` (well inside the 60 ms requirement): alpha 1 immediately, scale 0.4, then to 1.0 in 80 ms with Back.easeOut (overshoot 1.7, peaks about 1.1 near 55 ms). The ring is already correct and full on frame 1 because it reads `timer`. Reduced Motion: scale 1 from the first frame.

chunks.heading: 3.2 Timer ring (the clock)
chunks.text:
Remaining fraction `r = 1 - t`, drawn as an arc from 12 o'clock sweeping clockwise for `r` of a full turn, with the drained part removed from the END of the arc, i.e. the visible arc's start stays at 12 o'clock and its end retreats back toward it. It is empty (nothing drawn, track only) on the slam frame.
Colour by remaining time (never the only cue, the shrinking length is the signal):
- `timeLeft` above 450 ms: Cream #FFF6D6.
- 450 ms down to the urgency threshold: Mustard #E3A92B.
- Last 250 ms (urgency): Telegraph Red #FF3B30 (reserved for enemy attack warnings; this is exactly that: the slam is coming), ring width 6 to 8 px (inside radius 45 to 53, the track is 1 px thinner), and a thin 2 px Telegraph Red outer ring at radius 57, alpha 0.8 (shape cue: the bubble itself "swells a danger line").
Colour changes are hard steps (no flash).

chunks.heading: 3.3 Key cap rhythm (the verb)
chunks.text:
Needs 6 taps inside 900 ms, about 7 per second, so the cue shows an 8 Hz beat (125 ms period): cap goes down 3 px (side shrinks 4 px to 1 px) for 55 ms, back up in 70 ms (Back.easeOut). Real presses (attack or jump) always play the same down and up (50 ms down, 70 ms up) immediately, ignoring the beat, so response feels instant. The 8 Hz metronome only runs while the player has not pressed for 200 ms (a stalled player is exactly who needs the hint); a real press restarts it 200 ms later. Urgency state: metronome period 100 ms (10 Hz), and the whole bubble pulses scale 1.00 to 1.06 at 10 Hz.
- Every real press: the bubble also gets a micro bounce, scale 1.05 then 1.0 over 90 ms (Back.easeOut). Presses can come about 10 per second, so there is no white or cream brightness flash on a press (see 5, flash rate limit): only motion.
- Reduced Motion: cap and bubble static (no press animation, no pulse, no bounce). The cap shows its label with the side at 3 px.

chunks.heading: 3.4 Pips (the progress)
chunks.text:
`filled = floor(zed.grab.progress * breakTaps + 0.0001)`; if progress is between steps the next pip shows a partial fill (bottom up, height = fraction, 2 px minimum once above 0.1). Pips fill left to right.
- Empty pip: Dust #C9B79A fill, 2 px Dark Brown outline.
- Filled pip: Health Green #4C9A55 fill with a 2 px lighter top band #7BC47F.
- Next pip (the one to fill): outline Orange #F58A2A 2 px instead of Dark Brown, always on (static shape cue, also in Reduced Motion).
- On fill: the new pip starts bright (#A8E6AB) at scale 1.7 and settles to green at scale 1.0 over 100 ms (Back.easeOut). A brightness settle, not a flash.
- About to break (`filled >= breakTaps - 1`, the 5th pip filled): all filled pips use the brighter #7BC47F fill with a Spark Cream top band, and the last empty pip pulses its orange outline 2 to 3 px at 4 Hz (static orange outline in Reduced Motion). Pop on the 6th is the break (3.5).
- If the meter ever drains (gameplay may decay it), pips drain right to left with no animation. Spec assumes no decay (open question 4).

chunks.heading: 3.5 Break free (success)
chunks.text:
Trigger: the break state fires (6th tap). Zed drops (gameplay).
| Time | Spec |
|---|---|
| 0 | The 6th pip fills for one frame, then the bubble bursts: body and outline scale 1.0 to 1.25 in 70 ms (Quad.easeOut) with alpha 1 to 0; ring and pips vanish |
| 0 | 8 ring shards: 14 to 18 px long, 5 px thick strokes in Cream #FFF6D6 (4 of them Mustard #E3A92B), start at radius 52, fly outward to radius 96 over 260 ms (Cubic.easeOut), alpha 1 to 0. Pure shape, 8 primitives |
| 0 | Soft burst: Spark Cream disc radius 30 to 70, alpha 0.6 to 0 over 70 ms (Quad.easeOut). One burst, not repeated |
| 0 to 480 | Word "FREE!" in `FONTS.display` (Permanent Marker, fallback Impact) 34 px, Cream fill with 5 px Dark Brown stroke, no rotation. Pops 0.5 to 1.15 scale in 90 ms (Back.easeOut), 1.15 to 1.0 by 160 ms, then rises 18 px and fades to 0 from 260 to 480 ms (Quad.easeIn). World-anchored at the bubble's last position (it does not follow Zed, he has dropped) |
- Reduced Motion: no burst scale, no shards. Bubble fades 1 to 0 in 120 ms; "FREE!" shown static (scale 1, no rise) for 400 ms then fades 80 ms.
- Hit Flash Low: the soft burst disc is Sand #E8C27A, alpha 0.3, 160 ms (no cream core).

chunks.heading: 3.6 Slam (failed)
chunks.text:
Trigger: `PLAYER_SLAMMED` (slam frame, `timer >= holdMs`). The ring is empty on this frame. The cue must not fight the Wall Slam impact spec: it is on the top layer, small, and gone in 450 ms.
| Time | Spec |
|---|---|
| 0 | Ring empty, red. Three jagged crack lines across the body (Dark Brown 3 px, 40 to 60 px, jitter 4 px, from the key cap down through the pips) appear instantly. The bubble keeps shaking with the world camera (it is on the world camera, no extra shake) |
| 0 to 50 | Crack hold (about 3 frames) |
| 50 | The bubble splits into 8 pie wedges (the disc cut into 45 degree sectors, each drawn as a polygon of the arc, cream fill, 3 px Dark Brown outline, plus the tail as a 9th piece) that are blown away along `slamDir`: speed 520 to 900 px/s, cone +/-35 degrees around slamDir biased 25 degrees up, spin +/-8 rad/s, gravity 900, alpha 1 to 0 over 420 ms (last 40 percent of life) |
| 50 | Key cap and pips are drawn on the wedges they sit on (as part of the wedge, cut at the sector line) or drop straight down 60 px at gravity 900 with alpha 0 by 300 ms (simpler, recommended: the cap and pips fall as 2 loose pieces) |
| 470 | All gone |
- Reduced Motion: crack lines shown for 150 ms, then bubble fades out in 150 ms, no wedges.
- Hit Flash Low: no change (nothing here flashes).

chunks.heading: 3.7 Release (Dugan died or was stunned before the slam)
chunks.text: No fanfare: alpha 1 to 0 and scale 1.0 to 0.9 over 160 ms (Quad.easeIn). The ring and pips freeze at their current values while fading. Reduced Motion: fade only.

chunks.heading: 4. Placement and layering
chunks.text: World-anchored to Zed on the main (world) camera so it follows him as Dugan carries him (running-grab included), drawn at depth 5900: above the Wall Slam chunks and sparks (5800), below the HUD scene (a separate scene or camera, never covered). "FREE!" at depth 5950.

chunks.heading: 4. Placement and layering
chunks.text:
Position (screen = world minus camera scroll):
- Zed hangs about 120 px up and is about 90 px tall: `headTopY = zed.y - 120 - 90` (with `zed.y` = his shadow/feet line; if the sprite's `zed.z` holds the lift, use `zed.y - zed.z - 90`).
- Bubble centre: x = zed.x, y = `headTopY - tailLen(16) - gap(6) - 55` which is `zed.y - 287`. At a typical lane y 520 the bubble spans screen y 178 to 288 (centre 233).
- Clamp in screen space: x to [16 + 55, 1280 - 16 - 55] = [71, 1209]; y to at least 70 (HUD band) + 8 + 55 = 133 (add the 28 px of the hint pill while the hint is shown, so centre y at least 161). Clamp only moves the bubble; the tail always points from the bubble edge at Zed's head (tail length 10 to 22 px, shrinks if the clamp pushes it nearer).
- No horizontal offset: the bubble sits at least 20 px above Dugan's head (head top about zed.y - 192, the bubble's tail tip is at zed.y - 210), so Dugan's face is never covered.
- Positions are rounded to whole pixels every frame (pixel-art rule, no sub-pixel shimmer). No smoothing lag: the bubble is rigid with Zed.
- Camera zoom from Wall Slam (1.03) scales the bubble with the world, harmless.

chunks.heading: 5. Accessibility
chunks.text:
- Reduced Motion: no pop-in scale, no pulses, no bounce, no rhythm, no shards, no flying wedges, no shake. The ring still drains (it is state, not decoration) and pips still step in, static. The next-pip orange outline and the red last 250 ms stay.
- Hit Flash Low: no Spark Cream core flash on break (Sand at alpha 0.3 instead); no brightness pops on pips (the settle colour is the same as the final); Telegraph Red ring stays a solid colour (no blinking). There are no white flashes anywhere in this cue, and no element changes brightness more than 3 times per second (the pip settle is a 100 ms fade, and only the pop of scale repeats at tap rate).
- Colour is never the only signal: the ring shrinks (length), the pips count (shape), the cap presses (motion), the next pip has an orange outline, urgency thickens the ring and adds an outer line.
- Contrast: label Dark Brown on Orange about 6:1; Dark Brown outline on Cream about 11:1; ring Cream and Red on the Dark Brown track above 4.5:1.

chunks.heading: 6. First-time hint (decision)
chunks.text: Show "MASH!" on the pill above the bubble for the first grabs of a session until the player has broken free once, at most 3 times (module-level counter; resets on reload; never persisted, so it is not nagging a returning player). Worth it because it costs one pooled Text and the word reads in about 100 ms where the key cap alone does not say "many times". Text: Anton 18 px, Dark Brown on the Orange pill (contrast about 6:1), no rotation. Not shown if the clamp leaves no room (then skip it silently). Reduced Motion: same, static.

chunks.heading: 7. Implementation notes
chunks.text:
Suggested split (matches the pattern in `telegraphCueData.js`):
- `src/enemies/grabBreakCueData.js`: the `grabBreakCue` constants (below) plus a pure function `grabBreakCue({ timerMs, holdMs, progress, breakTaps, reduce })` returning `{ ring: {frac, color, widthPx, urgent}, pips: [0..1 x6], aboutToBreak, nextPip }`, and `keyLabel(code)`, `padLabel(index, padId)`. No Phaser.
- `src/enemies/GrabBreakCueFx.js`: owns one Graphics (depth 5900), two pooled Texts (label, word), and a 9-wedge pool. API: `show(zed, dugan)`, `update(dtMs, { timer, holdMs, progress, tapPressed })`, `onBreak()`, `onSlam(slamDir)`, `onRelease()`. `tapPressed` is true on the frame an attack or jump press is read in `held`, independent of whether the meter moved.
- Budget: 1 Graphics redrawn per frame (circle arcs, 6 pips, cap, tail), 2 Texts, up to 17 transient primitives on the success burst (8 shards, 1 disc, word), 9 wedges on the slam. Redraw only while the cue is alive.
- Audio hook (not specified here): a rising tick per tap (pitch up per pip), a bright chime on break, the existing slam thud on the slam frame.

chunks.heading: 8. Data
9. Open questions and playtest notes
chunks.text:
1. 8 Hz rhythm and 10 Hz urgency: needing 6 taps in 900 ms is about 7 per second, which is already at the edge of comfortable mashing, so the beat shown is a little above what is needed on purpose. Watch whether players try to match it or just mash; if the beat reads as a metronome to keep, slow it to 6.5 Hz.
2. Ring direction and the 250 ms red: check that the player does not read "ring shrinking" as "progress". If testers confuse it, flip the ring to a hand sweep with a small slam icon at 12 o'clock, or fill it instead of draining it.
3. Only Light is shown (J). Z, K, X and Space also work. Consider a small "ANY" tag, or a second tiny cap, if testers do not realise other buttons count. Left out for glance-readability.
4. Does the break meter decay between taps? The spec assumes no. If it decays, pips need a drain animation and `aboutToBreak` may flicker.
5. `zed.y`, the 120 px lift and the 90 px height are taken from the brief; the anchor formula may need `zed.z` or the held-sprite origin from `Zed.js`/`DuganGrab`. Verify in the scene that the tail lands on his head.
6. The bubble is on the world camera so it shakes and zooms with the Wall Slam. If the world camera scrolls hard during the running-grab catch, check the clamp does not jitter; fall back to rigid world position with a 1-frame-lag clamp.
7. First-time hint: 3 shows until the first break might be too many or too few; try 2.
8. Gamepad glyph for PlayStation pads is a drawn square; if the id sniffing misfires, default to `X`.
9. Audio is not covered (hooks listed in 7).

chunks.heading: 10. Assumptions
chunks.text:
- `holdMs` and `breakTaps` are read at runtime from the grab state, so the cue still matches if Dugan's tuning changes.
- Fonts are loaded by `waitForFonts()` before any Text is created (Anton and Permanent Marker are in `FONT_LOADS`).
- The HUD is on its own scene or camera above or apart from the world camera.
- Telegraph Red is allowed here because the bubble warns of an enemy attack (the slam); no Brick Red or red-orange is used on enemy bodies.
- The key cap letter is 28 px Anton; confirm it stays crisp against the integer-scale pixel look when the bubble is scaled by the pop.

chunks.heading: Revision (owner request, after playtest feedback)
chunks.text:
- **Break taps are now 7** (`GRAB_CONFIG.breakTaps`); the pips follow it (7 pips, "about to break" from the 6th).
- **The ring is now a clock, not a meter.** A draining ring could be read as progress. The time that has gone now fills **red** clockwise behind a small hand; the time left stays cream, then mustard in the last 450 ms. The pips are the only green. Rule: fill the green before the red closes the ring. The hand reaches 12 o'clock on the slam frame. The urgency state (last 250 ms) keeps the thicker ring, the outer red line and the 10 Hz pulse.
- The key cap shows both attack keys, "J / K"; jump does not count.

chunks.heading: Dugan Mega Stomp (art and feedback spec)
chunks.text: Status: PROPOSED starting values for playtest. Owner: art-direction-agent. Extends the Ground Stomp of "Brick" Dugan (Level 1 mini-boss). Gameplay numbers (700 ms wind-up, slam at +150 ms, 850 px/s to 760 px per side, lane-wide, airborne at 30 px or more is safe, parry negates, 14 damage, 360 knockback) are fixed inputs and are not changed here. Flat vector, all shapes drawn in code, no new image files. Times are ms from the start of the wind-up. Slam = 850.

chunks.heading: 1. Intent
chunks.text: The player should feel a 192 px steel man lift off, drop, and break the street open, and should read one thing: a bright wall of broken ground is rolling toward Zed along the whole lane, and the answer is to leave the floor as it touches him. Cold Rust grey gathers (wind-up), warm broken pavement answers (wave), so "Rust power" and "the city taking the hit" stay in the project's two colour families. Two thin cold ghost pulses go out first, then the real hot one, on an even 350 ms beat, so the player learns the speed and shape of the wave before it counts. The wave is drawn as a lane-wide wall, not a circle, because its hit rule ignores depth: the shape tells the truth about the hitbox, so side-stepping in depth visibly cannot work.

chunks.heading: 2. Timeline
chunks.text: Distance d from Dugan's feet. The front reaches a target at 850 + 1.18 x d ms (d 150 = 1026, d 300 = 1203, d 500 = 1438, d 760 = 1744).

chunks.heading: 2. Timeline
chunks.text:
| Time (ms) | Player sees | Camera |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Wind-up starts. Dark flattened ellipse fades in under Dugan (rx 70 growing to 230, ry = 0.3 rx), cold Steel rim. Two thin red dashed "reach gates" fade in at x0 +/- 760, lane tall, so Zed knows how far it reaches | Soft rumble 0.0006 |
| 150 | Ghost pulse A: thin cold slate line, lane tall, travels out from Dugan to 250 px at 850 px/s (294 ms), same shape as the real wave, harmless, alpha 0.5 | rumble |
| 350 | Disc about half grown, Dugan crouched | rumble rises to 0.0012 |
| 500 | Ghost pulse B, identical to A. Beat is 150, 500, 850 (350 ms apart, 2.9 Hz, under the 3 per second limit; thin low-contrast lines, not flashes) | rumble 0.0012 |
| 550 to 700 | Disc rim shifts Steel to Visor Cyan and thickens 3 to 5 px: "now" cue. Disc stops growing | rumble |
| 700 | Leap starts (clip frames of the rise). Disc holds, Dugan's shadow shrinks to 50 percent. Wind-up ends (700 ms, well over the 300 ms minimum) | 0.0020 for 150 ms |
| 850 | SLAM. Attacker hit-stop 90 ms (target 0). One cream flattened core flash at his feet (90 ms), hot ring bursts out, 18 chunks and 14 dust puffs, 6 big radial cracks. The two wave fronts spawn | Peak shake (see 4) |
| 850 to 1744 | Two fronts travel out at 850 px/s. Behind each: Ember band, dust trail, cracks lighting and fading. Ahead: dirt pops warn of the front. Disc turns scorch brown and fades 850 to 1350 | Decaying shake, ends 1740 |
| 1544 to 1744 | Fronts fade (alpha ramp from d 560 to 760). Reach gates fade with them | last tail |
| 1744 to 2450 | Last cracks and dust fade. Nothing left on screen | none |

chunks.heading: 3.1 Telegraph (0 to 850)
chunks.text:
- Disc: flattened ellipse at feet, rx 70 to 230 over 0 to 700 (Quad.easeOut), ry = 0.3 rx. Fill Rust Ink #14181C, alpha 0 to 0.45 (Sine.easeIn). Rim stroke 3 px Steel #7C8A96 alpha 0.8, then Visor Cyan #4FB3D9 and 5 px from 550 to 700. Cold and Rust-coded, no red fill, so it is not the charge strip (#D23A2E translucent strip) and not the parry ring (orange, closing, over the head).
- Ghost pulses: lane-tall vertical line (y 440 to 700), 4 px, Steel #7C8A96 alpha 0.5, no teeth, no glow.
- Reach gates: dashed vertical lines (dash 18, gap 14), 3 px, Telegraph Red #FF3B30 (reserved warning use is correct here), alpha 0 to 0.4 over 300 ms, thin so they do not read as a filled floor strip.
- Close-range rule (for the designer): anyone within about 100 px is hit within 120 ms of the slam and cannot react to the front. They must jump on the leap cue (cyan rim, Dugan leaving the ground). See open questions.

chunks.heading: 3.2 Wave front, per side (850 to 1744)
chunks.text:
Drawn in screen space, lane tall (y 440 to 700, 20 px margin each side), travelling away from Dugan. Layers from the leading edge backward:
1. Leading line, 6 px wide, Spark Cream #FFF6D6, alpha 1. This is the single truth for the jump: feet must be 30 px or more off the floor as this line crosses Zed.
2. Crest teeth: 12 triangles along the line, one per 22 px of y, base 14 px, height 34 px (taller than the 30 px threshold, so "clear the teeth" equals "be safe"), pointing up and leaning 8 px toward travel. Fill Sand #E8C27A, 2 px outline #2E1F16. Height stays 34 until the fade starts.
3. Ember band: 26 px behind the line, Ember #F58A2A, alpha 0.8 at the line to 0.3 at the back (linear).
4. Dust trail: 80 px band behind the Ember band, Dust #C9B79A alpha 0.35 to 0.
5. Warning dirt pops ahead: 1 small 2x18 px Warm Brown #6B4423 tick every 30 px, from 30 to 120 px ahead of the front (about 100 ms of look-ahead), alpha 0.5, fading as the front reaches them.
Alpha: full to d 560, then linear to 0 at d 760. Only the leading line is the hit test; the band and trail are cosmetic.
Hot orange justification: Ember #F58A2A is already pending in hit-feedback-spec 7.5 and is the "broken ground glows" colour, not an enemy-body colour. The wave avoids Telegraph Red, Enemy Critical and Finisher Orange #FFA41C (parry).

chunks.heading: 3.3 Cracks, dust, debris
chunks.text:
- Cracks: a 3-segment jagged polyline spawned each time the front passes a 40 px station (19 per side), random y in 460 to 680, length 30 to 60 px, flattened to the floor. Core line 3 px #2E1F16 alpha 0.6 (hold 300 ms then fade 400, 700 total). Inner glow line 1 px Ember #F58A2A alpha 0.9 to 0 over 400 ms. At the slam: 6 big radial cracks, 120 to 200 px long, same look, life 900 ms.
- Dust: 1 puff per 38 px station per side (20 per side), ellipse 24 to 48 px wide, h = 0.8 w, random y in lane, rises 30 px, alpha 0.5 to 0, life 500 to 700, colours Dust #C9B79A 60 percent, Sand #E8C27A 25 percent, Warm Brown #6B4423 15 percent. Slam burst: 14 puffs, 40 to 80 px, life 700 to 900.
- Debris: slam 18 chunks (rects and triangles 6 to 14 px), speed 300 to 700, cone 55 to 125 degrees up, gravity 1400, one floor bounce at restitution 0.35, life 700 to 1000, colours Warm Brown 40 percent, Dark Brown #2E1F16 25 percent, Dust 20 percent, Steel #7C8A96 15 percent. Along the front: 1 chunk per 60 px per side (12 per side), thrown up (vy -380 to -520), life 450. Debris layer follows hit-feedback-spec 7.3.3 (layer B, depth 5800); floor FX (disc, cracks, band) sit below characters and above ground shadows.
- Slam core: Spark Cream flattened ellipse, rx 80 to 200, 90 ms, alpha 0.8, Quad.easeOut. Slam ring: flattened ellipse stroke 8 px, Spark Cream to Ember, rx 30 to 260 over 260 ms, Cubic.easeOut, alpha 1 to 0.
- Optional reward: when Zed is airborne as the front passes under him, 6 small dust puffs at his feet. No flash.

chunks.heading: 4. Mega screen shake
chunks.text:
Phaser applies constant intensity per call and ignores a new shake while one runs unless `force` is true, so call each keyframe with force true. Keyframes `[atMs, durationMs, intensity]`:
`[0,350,0.0006] [350,350,0.0012] [700,150,0.0020] [850,90,0.018] [940,110,0.013] [1050,140,0.009] [1190,170,0.005] [1360,200,0.0025] [1560,180,0.0012]`
- Slam shake runs 850 to 1740 (0.89 s, under the 1.4 s cap), with decay of about 0.7x per step. Peak 0.018 is about 23 px, 4x the biggest existing shake (0.0045). Justified because it is the loudest event in Level 1, happens once per stomp, and the peak lasts only 90 ms; by 1050 it is already at 0.009, so the front stays readable while the player decides. The wave reads the same with the shake off because the front is positioned in world space.
- Screen Shake Light: every intensity x0.5 (peak 0.009), same timings. Off: no keyframes.
- Reduced Motion: treated as shake Off (no camera calls), dust and debris counts halved, ghost pulses and pops kept. The wave, cracks and teeth are unchanged so the move stays fully readable.
- Hit Flash Low: skip the cream core flash (replace with the same ellipse at alpha 0.35 over 200 ms, Sand #E8C27A); leading line colour Spark Cream becomes Sand #E8C27A; slam ring alpha 0.5 and width 4; Ember glow alpha x0.5; ghost pulses alpha 0.35. Persistent lines are not flashes, so the jump cue stays at full contrast.
- Recommend the HUD stays on its own camera so it does not shake.

chunks.heading: 5. Data
6. Open questions and playtest notes
chunks.text:
1. Zed's jump airtime and take-off delay are not given here. The 30 px window must stay above 30 px for long enough to cover the front passing his hurtbox plus input error; if airtime is under about 450 ms, jump timing will feel unforgiving. Needs a number from Player Combos.
2. Close range: a player within about 100 px is hit within 120 ms of the slam and cannot react to the front. Options (owner call, not decided): spawn the fronts at his body edge (about +/-70 px), or accept it as "you stood too close". I did not change the gameplay numbers.
3. Reach gates (red dashed lines) are my addition and use Telegraph Red; cut them if the lane gets too busy. Camera view is 1280 px, so the far gate may be off-screen.
4. Parry: the spec says parry negates, but not whether the existing orange closing ring shows. I left it off so the jump reads as the answer; a player who parries by instinct has no cue. Confirm.
5. Peak shake 0.018 (about 23 px) is a guess; try 0.012 to 0.02. Phaser shake is random per frame, so test it on a real display.
6. Cost: about 140 simple shapes alive at peak (cracks 44, dust 54, debris 42), above the 60 cap in hit-feedback-spec 7.3 which covers hit particles only. Use a separate pool.
7. Hit-stop 90 ms freezes Dugan only; the wave keeps running in real time. Combined with the 80 ms Zed hurt stop the cap (150) still holds.
8. Ember #F58A2A and Sand #E8C27A as Rust-attack colours need owner approval (Ember is already pending in hit-feedback-spec 7.5). The wave band is hot-warm on purpose; if the owner wants it colder, swap the band to Light Steel #BFC8CF.
9. The wave front is lane tall (y 440 to 700) rather than a flattened ellipse, deliberately, so it matches the depth-ignoring hitbox. Floor discs, rings and cracks still use the 0.3 ratio.

chunks.heading: Dugan Wall Slam impact (art and feedback spec)
chunks.text:
Status: PROPOSED starting values for playtest. Owner: art-direction-agent. Covers the moment "Brick" Dugan's Grab and Wall Slam (and the charge-catch grab) slams Zed into the ground. Feedback only: damage, knockback (640 px/s, fast decay), 700 ms lying time, Dugan's 110 ms hit-stop and every other gameplay number are fixed inputs and are not changed here. Flat vector, all shapes drawn in code, no new image files. Times are ms from the `PLAYER_SLAMMED` event, so the impact is t = 0. There is no wind-up: Dugan's hold is the wind-up.
Input: `PLAYER_SLAMMED { attackerId, damage, slamDir (+1 / -1 toward the wall), x, y }`. x0, y0 = Zed's feet at impact. dir = slamDir. All floor shapes are flattened ellipses (height ratio 0.3), same as the Mega Stomp.

chunks.heading: 1. Intent
chunks.text:
Mega Stomp is a long rolling wave you read and dodge. Wall Slam is the opposite: a short, brutal, compressed jolt that has already happened. The player should feel one hard crunch (about 0.4 s of shake, not a rumble), see the street split under Zed in a star, see a hot ring shove dust and pebbles outward, and see one long crack race ahead of him in the direction he is about to be thrown. Then it settles: a dark dent under his body, a skid groove behind him, and dust, while he lies there for 700 ms. Same colour families as the stomp (warm broken pavement answers cold Rust power), but no wave front, no teeth, no red: nothing here is a hit test or a warning, so nothing looks like one.
Readability rules: every floor shape sits on the floor layer (depth 440, behind Zed and every fighter), so Zed, his lying pose and the HUD are never covered. The only near-white area is the core flash, 70 ms, flattened and under him. Top-layer pieces (depth 5800) are chunks and sparks only, each 14 px or smaller.

chunks.heading: 2. Timeline (ms from impact)
chunks.text:
| Time | Player sees | Camera |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Dent snaps in under Zed. Core flash (cream, 70 ms). Ring bursts out. Star cracks appear at 15 percent length and run out. 14 chunks, 10 sparks, 12 dust puffs launch. Pebbles and ring dust start moving with the ring. Edge vignette snaps to peak | Shake peak 0.015. Punch-in to 1.03 in 60 ms |
| 0 to 140 | Long cracks and the slide crack grow to full length (Expo.easeOut, the slide crack is the fastest). Spark at the slide crack's growing tip | shake 0.015 then 0.011 |
| 70 | Core flash gone. Ripple 1 starts | |
| 120 | Ripple 2 starts. Zed slides at about 640 px/s: skid groove and slide dust begin | shake 0.0075 |
| 240 | Main ring gone. Ring dust and pebbles still travelling | shake 0.0045 from 200 |
| 300 | Zoom back to 1.0 (260 ms Sine.easeInOut, from 60 to 320). Vignette gone at 400 | shake 0.0022 from 290, ends 380 |
| 350 | Dent holds until here, then fades | none |
| 900 | Dent gone. Slide dust and chunks done by about 1000 | |
| 1200 | Cracks gone (Zed stands up about 700 ms after the slide). Nothing left on screen | |

chunks.heading: 3.1 Dent and dust bowl (floor layer)
chunks.text: Flattened ellipse at (x0, y0), rx 70 snapping to 110 over 90 ms (Quad.easeOut), ry = 0.3 rx. Fill Dark Brown #2E1F16, alpha 0.55. Rim stroke 3 px Warm Brown #6B4423 alpha 0.6 (the "lip" of the bowl). Holds 350 ms, then alpha to 0 by 900 (Quad.easeIn). It sits under Zed's lying body so the silhouette stays readable against it. Not red, not cold: it reads as pressed earth.

chunks.heading: 3.2 Core flash and ring
chunks.text:
- Core: Spark Cream #FFF6D6 flattened ellipse, rx 40 to 120 over 70 ms (Quad.easeOut), alpha 0.7 to 0. Under Zed.
- Ring: flattened ellipse stroke, rx 20 to 210 over 240 ms (Cubic.easeOut), width 6 to 2 px, colour Cream #FFF6D6 until 35 percent of life then Ember #F58A2A, alpha 1 to 0.
- Ripples: two thin trailing rings behind the main ring, Dust #C9B79A, 2 px, alpha 0.35 to 0. Ripple 1 starts at 70 ms, rx 30 to 300, life 380 ms. Ripple 2 starts at 120 ms, rx 30 to 380, life 460 ms. Both Cubic.easeOut. They carry the "area" feel past the star and are cheap (two strokes).

chunks.heading: 3.3 Cracks: star, area-wide, and the slide crack (floor layer)
chunks.text:
Look for every crack: core line 3 px Dark Brown #2E1F16 alpha 0.7, plus a 1 px Ember #F58A2A glow line alpha 0.8 that fades over the first 250 ms, so the crack looks freshly broken then goes cold. Cracks are jagged polylines (segments of 40 to 60 px, jitter +/-5 px in x, +/-3 px in y). Vertical component is scaled 0.3 like all floor shapes, and every point is clamped to y 445 to 695. Hold 700 ms, then fade 500 ms (life 1200).
1. Short radial cracks: 4, evenly spaced with +/-0.25 rad jitter, length 90 to 140 px.
2. Long radial cracks: 2, one on each side of the screen (angle 0 and 180 deg, +/-0.2 rad), length 220 to 300 px. These carry the damage across the area.
3. Slide crack: 1, along slamDir, starts at (x0, y0 + 2), length 360 px, nearly straight (jitter +/-3 px, y drift at most 8 px), grows from 0 to full length in 140 ms (Expo.easeOut). Its tip emits 1 spark per 35 ms while growing (4 sparks total, small, counted in the spark budget). It leads ahead of the sliding body and shows where he is going.
4. Branches: 3 total, one on each long radial and one on the slide crack, at 40 to 55 percent of length, +/-35 deg off the parent, length 40 percent of the parent, same look.
5. Arena clamp: if the crack would pass the arena's walkable x range, cut it at the edge (data flag `clampToArenaX`).

chunks.heading: 3.4 Chunks (top layer, depth 5800)
chunks.text: 14 chunks, rects and triangles 6 to 12 px (40 percent triangles), spawn at x0 +/-24, y0 +/-8, speed 260 to 620, cone 60 to 120 deg up, gravity 1400, one floor bounce at restitution 0.3, life 600 to 900, fade over the last 30 percent. 4 of the 14 get a horizontal bias of +0.3 along slamDir so debris leans with the slide. Colours Warm Brown #6B4423 40 percent, Dark Brown #2E1F16 25 percent, Dust #C9B79A 20 percent, Steel #7C8A96 15 percent.

chunks.heading: 3.5 Sparks (top layer)
chunks.text: 10 sparks (include the 4 from the slide crack tip, so 6 at the contact point). Rotated rect, length 14 to 20, thickness 3, 3-sample trail, cone +/-30 deg around slamDir biased 20 deg up, speed 420 to 760, gravity 900, life 220 to 320. Colour by life with the project's hot-to-cool ramp (hit-feedback-spec 7.3.2): White #FFFFFF, Gold #FFD24A at 0.2, Ember #F58A2A at 0.5, Rust brown #9C5A2E at 0.8. White is a single frame on spawn, not a flash. Scrape sparks while sliding: 1 every 90 ms while slide speed is above 200 px/s, 3 at most, same look at 60 percent size, flung opposite to slamDir.

chunks.heading: 3.6 Shockwave shoves dust and pebbles (floor layer, small)
chunks.text:
- Ring dust: 16 puffs placed evenly around the ellipse at radius 40, each travels out with the ring to rx 200 over 420 ms (Quad.easeOut), size 26 to 44 (grows x1.3), height ratio 0.8, alpha 0.5 to 0, colours Dust 60 percent, Sand 25, Warm Brown 15. This is the visible "ring pushes dust" beat: the dust trails slightly behind the ring edge.
- Pebbles: 14 tiny 3 to 5 px Warm Brown or Dust squares that were "lying" at radius 30 to 160 from the impact at a random angle. At the moment the ring passes their radius (ring radius equals their radius) each hops: vz 120 to 260 px/s, then lands, drifting outward 60 to 140 px/s, gravity 1000, life 400. Result: small stuff visibly jumps as the ring passes, nothing is pre-drawn.
- Burst dust: 12 big puffs 40 to 72 px, spawn x0 +/-70, life 650 to 850, rise 24, alpha 0.55 to 0.

chunks.heading: 3.7 Slide trail (while Zed skids)
chunks.text:
Reads Zed's real x each frame, so it follows whatever the slide physics does. Active while slide speed is above 120 px/s.
- Skid groove: a 3 px Dark Brown #2E1F16 line at alpha 0.35 from x0 to Zed's current x, 2 px below his feet y, 5 px of jitter free. Stays 400 ms after he stops, then fades over 300 ms.
- Slide dust: 1 puff per 45 ms behind him (opposite slamDir), size 24 to 40, height ratio 0.8, rise 14, alpha 0.4 to 0, life 400 to 550, Dust and Sand. Maximum 10 puffs over the slide.

chunks.heading: 3.8 Edge vignette (screen space, optional but recommended)
chunks.text: Four screen-edge bands drawn as 6 nested rectangular frames (each 14 px wide, 84 px of total depth), colour Dark Brown #2E1F16, alpha from 0.30 (outermost) stepping to 0.05 (innermost). The whole thing multiplies by an envelope: 0 to 1 in 30 ms, then 1 to 0 over 370 ms (Quad.easeOut, ends at 400). Peak effective outer alpha is 0.30. It is a darkening, not a bright flash, so it does not count toward the flash-rate limit. It lives in screen space (scrollFactor 0) on the main camera only, below the HUD, so it never dims the HUD (see open question 2).

chunks.heading: 3.9 Camera punch-in (optional)
chunks.text: Zoom 1.0 to 1.03 in 60 ms (Quad.easeOut), then back to 1.0 over 260 ms (Sine.easeInOut). Aim at Zed's x0 y0 (the camera should pan its view centre a maximum of 40 px toward him, which keeps him inside the frame). Gives "the world hits you" without a long rumble.

chunks.heading: 4. Slam screen shake
chunks.text:
Phaser camera.shake is constant intensity per call and ignores a new shake while one runs unless `force` is true, so run each keyframe with force true. Keyframes `[atMs, durationMs, intensity]`:
`[0,50,0.015] [50,70,0.011] [120,80,0.0075] [200,90,0.0045] [290,90,0.0022]`
- Peak 0.015 (about 19 px) is below the Mega Stomp's 0.018 and above the old 0.012. Total length 380 ms, versus 890 ms for the Mega Stomp. It replaces the scene's current 320 ms at 0.012 (the scene must not run both).
- How it differs in feel: the Mega Stomp is a loud thing that arrives and then rolls away (about 0.9 s, 9 steps, with a rumble leading up to it). This is a compressed jolt: a 50 ms hit at 0.015 with the biggest drop first (0.015 to 0.011 to 0.0075 in 120 ms), then a short ringing tail, finished before Zed has even stopped sliding. About 3 frames at peak, so it reads as one hard crack, not a quake. Total shake energy (intensity x duration) is about a fifth of the Mega Stomp's.
- Screen Shake Light: all intensities x0.5 (peak 0.0075), same timings, zoom delta halved (1.015). Off: no shake keyframes and no zoom.
- Reduced Motion: treated as shake Off (no shake, no zoom), pebbles, chunks, sparks, ring dust, burst dust and slide dust halved. The ring, cracks, dent, vignette (at 0.6 alpha) and skid groove are kept, so the slam still reads clearly and nothing is lost for the player. Cracks appear at full length with no growth animation in this mode.
- Hit Flash Low: skip the cream core flash and replace it with the same ellipse in Sand #E8C27A at alpha 0.3 over 160 ms; ring colours Cream to Sand #E8C27A, alpha 0.6, width 3; sparks start at Gold (no White stop); vignette x0.6; glow lines alpha x0.5. Zoom and shake are not flashes and stay on their own settings.
- The scene keeps Dugan's 110 ms hit-stop on Dugan only. The FX run on real time and are not frozen by it. The HUD should stay on its own camera so it does not shake or zoom.

chunks.heading: 5. Budget
chunks.text: Peak live pieces: chunks 14, sparks 10, burst dust 12, ring dust 16, pebbles 14, slide dust 10, cracks 10 (4 + 2 + 1 + 3 branches), ripples 2, ring 1, core 1, dent 1, groove 1: about 92 at the busiest moment (around 150 ms), 100 hard cap (drop slide dust, then pebbles first). All primitives, 2 Graphics (floor 440, top 5800) plus one screen-space Graphics for the vignette.

chunks.heading: 6. Data
7. Open questions and playtest notes
chunks.text:
1. Zed's slide distance is not given (640 px/s decaying fast). The slide crack is a fixed 360 px so it should lead him; if he slides much farther, or the wall is closer than 360 px, make it min(360, distance to arena edge) (the `clampToArenaX` flag handles the second case).
2. HUD depth and camera: the vignette and zoom assume the HUD is on its own camera or above depth 5800. If the HUD shares the main camera, the zoom will scale it (cut the zoom) and the vignette must be drawn below it. Needs a check against the scene.
3. Camera follow: a zoom while the camera is scrolling may fight the follow logic. If it looks bad, cut the zoom first; it is optional.
4. Peak 0.015 (about 19 px) is a guess; try 0.012 to 0.017. At the same time make sure the 380 ms tail does not look like the old 320 ms constant shake.
5. Chunks on the top layer can briefly cross Zed's body (14 px or smaller, under 900 ms). If they hide his hurt pose, move the chunks to depth just above Zed's y instead.
6. Damage scaling: one fixed intensity. If Dugan's slam damage varies, scale shake and ring radius by damage / reference (not proposed here since there is only one damage value).
7. The vignette is dark brown on purpose (not Telegraph Red #FF3B30, not white). If the owner wants Zed's hurt to read warmer, use Ember at alpha 0.15, but that is a flash risk and needs sign-off.
8. Audio is not covered: a deep thud with a short crack layer on t = 0 and a gravel scatter at 150 ms would match this timing.
9. Same event is used for the charge-catch grab, so there is only one version; if the catch should be lighter, use Light-scale values as the data (a `intensityScale` multiplier on everything).

chunks.heading: Rust Enemy Sprite Specs (all 14 units)
chunks.text:
Owner: art-direction-agent. Status: DRAFT for owner approval. Nothing in this file is final art. The generated `assets/sprites/rust-*-placeholder.svg` boxes have been deleted. Delivered PNG art now exists for Bruisers, Rangers (Watchers), Specialists (Copper Fangs) and Breaker Type 2; units with no delivered art are `null` in `assets/asset-keys.json`.
Sources of truth, read in full: `content/enemies/rust-roster.json` (grunt), `content/enemies/rust-gdd-units.json` (the other 13), `design/art/style-guide.md`, `design/art/hit-feedback-spec.md`, `design/art/asset-manifest.md`, `assets/asset-keys.json`, `src/player/zedVisual.js` and `assets/sprites/zed/` (Zed's loading convention). Telegraph and attack timings below are copied from the unit JSON; where a move has no timing in the JSON the cell says "not set" and the enemy owner must set it (rule: never below 300 ms).

chunks.heading: 0. Decisions that need owner approval (summary)
chunks.text:
1. Phase-2 "red" glows (Calder suit, Voss drones) break the no-red-on-enemies rule. APPROVED by the owner: Overload Violet `#8E5BFF` with Overload Ice `#BFF4FF` core. See section 3.1.
2. KO is a knockdown, never a kill. Spec in section 3.2. The boss defeat beat (what the player sees when a boss reaches 0 HP) is a narrative question for the owner.
3. Art style for Rust. The style guide says Rust stays flat vector next to pixel Zed, but Open Question 1 is still open. This spec is written for flat vector delivered as PNG. If the owner picks pixel art, see section 1.2 note.
4. Copper Fang's "copper" gauntlets cannot be copper-orange (red-orange ban). Recommended muted Bronze `#9A8466`. Section 2.3.
5. Grunt display height (96 px figure) is shorter than Zed (frame 120 px on screen, figure unmeasured here, roughly 100 to 110 px). Confirm in-engine that the grunt does not read as a child next to Zed. Sizes below keep the grunt as the base (1.00).
6. Unit assumptions marked "ASSUMPTION" in the unit sections (Copper Fang phase-2 shield, Hologram attack is a punch only, Cordon has no Jab Combo, Varr stance colours, Wren Rooftop Execution shown as a knockdown dive).
7. (Resolved) The grunt placeholder SVG, which had a baked ground-shadow ellipse, has been deleted.

chunks.heading: 1.1 Frame size, scale, feet anchor
chunks.text:
- Frames are authored at final on-screen size. Display scale is 1.0 for every enemy, with one exception: if Rust becomes pixel art (1.2).
- One canvas size per unit, used for every state and both facings, so the engine never needs a per-clip origin table (Zed needs one because its clips have mixed canvases; enemies must not).
- Feet anchor: the lowest standing-foot pixel row is `frameHeight * 15/16 - 1` (128 frame: row 119, matching the grunt placeholder). Engine origin for every ground unit is `(0.5, 0.9375)`, horizontally centred on the body mass at rest. Flyers (drones, MegaDrone): the same baseline row marks the ground point under the unit; the body floats 20 px above it in Idle, bob up to 3 px is authored into the Idle loop.
- Keep the figure inside the canvas in every pose, including raised weapons, lunges and the extended-arm poses. Leave 4 px of empty border on every side.
- No ground shadow in any frame (the game draws the flat 25 percent ellipse).

chunks.heading: 1.1 Frame size, scale, feet anchor
chunks.text: Rationale: Varr and Voss are near Zed's height so the duel reads as equals; the Breaker and Calder are the only units clearly bigger than Zed (heavy-enemy cue); the Watcher and Wren are slimmer, not shorter, so their lean silhouette is the cue.

chunks.heading: 1.2 Style
chunks.text:
- Flat vector look: 2 to 3 flat tones per colour, no gradients, no textures, no dithering. Outline `#14181C` (Rust Ink), 4 px at 128 px frame height, scaled proportionally (192 frame: 6 px, 256 frame: 8 px, 64 frame: 2 px). Light from top left.
- Deliver as PNG (transparent, straight alpha). Vector source (SVG or layered file) is kept alongside under `assets/sprites/_src/<unit>/` if the artist wants, but the game loads PNG only.
- Silhouette first: every unit must be identifiable as a solid black shape. Boxy, symmetrical, straight edges (Zed is round and warm).
- NOTE if the owner chooses pixel art for Rust: author at Zed's pixel density (1 source px = 2.5 screen px), so frame sizes above divide by 2.5 (grunt about 51x51, rounded up to a multiple of 4), display scale 2.5, nearest-neighbour filtering, 1 px outline `#14181C`. Counts, states and naming do not change.

chunks.heading: 1.3 Facing
chunks.text:
- Side view only, east and west textures per frame, same as Zed (`ZED_SPRITE.dir`: right = east, left = west). The engine swaps textures; never `flipX`.
- West may be generated as a mirror export of east (units are boxy and symmetrical) but the artist must check asymmetric props after mirroring: Calder's hammer arm, Copper Fang's shield/hook sides, Varr's gauntlet/emitter sides, Watcher's rifle. The prop side may swap after mirroring, which is acceptable; text, serial numbers and logos must be re-set so they do not read backwards. Do not ship the 6 other Zed directions (south, north etc.); not needed.

chunks.heading: 1.4 Folders, files, keys (mirrors Zed's layout)
chunks.text:
Zed layout, for reference: `assets/sprites/zed/<State>/rotations/<dir>.png` and `assets/sprites/zed/<Folder>/animations/<AnimName>/<dir>/frame_000.png`.
Enemy layout:

chunks.heading: 1.4 Folders, files, keys (mirrors Zed's layout)
chunks.text:
- Unit folder: sprite key with dots replaced by dashes: `assets/sprites/rust-grunt/`, `assets/sprites/rust-iron-line-cordon/`, `rust-breaker`, `rust-watcher`, `rust-copper-fang`, `rust-halden-varr`, `rust-overseer-voss`, `rust-overseer-calder`, `rust-overseer-wren`, `rust-drone`, `rust-megadrone`, `rust-hologram`, `rust-elite-drone`.
- State folder (PascalCase, underscore separates state and move): `Idle`, `Walk`, `Hit`, `Ko`, `Telegraph`, `Attack`, `Telegraph_GauntletSmash`, `Attack_GauntletSmash`, `Hold_SteamBurst`, `Transition_Phase2`, and so on. Phase-2 variants carry a `P2_` prefix: `P2_Idle`, `P2_Telegraph_RustCollapse`.
- Key pose (one static image per state, used for the Phaser texture before animations register, and as a fallback): `assets/sprites/<unit>/<State>/rotations/east.png` and `west.png`. For Telegraph states the key pose is the peak wind-up frame; for Attack states it is the strike frame; for other states it is frame 000.
- Animation frames: `assets/sprites/<unit>/<State>/animations/<state-lowercase>/<dir>/frame_000.png`, `frame_001.png`, ... (3-digit, zero based, same as `zedFramePath`).
- Example, Breaker smash wind-up: `assets/sprites/rust-breaker/Telegraph_GauntletSmash/rotations/east.png` and `.../Telegraph_GauntletSmash/animations/telegraph_gauntlet-smash/west/frame_004.png`. The animations subfolder name is the folder name lowercased with moves in kebab case.
- Phaser texture key (like `zedTextureKey`): `<spriteKey>.<state>[.<move>][.p2].<dir>`; frame key adds `.<i>`. Animation key (what `asset-keys.json` lists): `rust.breaker.telegraph.gauntlet-smash`, `rust.copper-fang.p2.telegraph.hook`. Direction suffix `.east` / `.west` is appended by the loader exactly as Zed's (`zed.run.east`). Move ids are kebab case (`gauntlet-smash`).
- The grunt's existing default clips keep their keys (`rust.grunt.telegraph`, `rust.grunt.attack`); later grunt moves add `.headbutt`, `.jab-combo`.
- `assets/asset-keys.json` lists every animation key per unit (generated from the same table as this spec). The enemy-owner's data table (like `gruntData.js`) maps its states to these keys.

chunks.heading: 1.5 Clips, tempo and the telegraph rule
chunks.text:
- Nominal fps for authoring: Idle 6, Walk 10, Hit 12, Ko 10, Attack 20, Hold loops 6. Telegraph clips are authored at a nominal 8 fps but the engine stretches them to the unit's `telegraphMs` (`anims.timeScale = (frames / fps) / (telegraphMs / 1000)`, the same technique `zedVisual.js` uses for punches and parry). So artists draw poses, not timings.
- Telegraph clip construction (all units, all moves), per `hit-feedback-spec.md` section 3:
 1. Frame 1 already differs from Idle in silhouette. The cue starts at t = 0, not after a lead-in.
 2. The peak pose (last frame) is reached by about the first third of the wind-up and then holds. Totals: the peak pose is on screen for at least 300 ms for any wind-up of 450 ms or more; for the 320 to 400 ms wind-ups (Fang Jab, Watcher baton, Varr Authority Strike, Wren GrappleDash) the whole wind-up is at least 300 ms by the JSON floor and the peak holds for the remaining 60 percent.
 3. The peak pose reads in solid-black silhouette alone: the weapon or limb must leave the body outline (arm cocked back, braces overhead, rifle raised), never an interior detail.
 4. Outline is 1 px wider (scaled: 5 px at 128 frame) on every frame of a Telegraph clip. This is baked, it is cue 2 of the hit-feedback spec.
 5. Never bake red or orange anywhere. The orange finisher ring (`#FFA41C`), ground danger zones, scan lines and hit-flash are all runtime effects. Keep slate/steel mid-tones and avoid large near-white areas on the body, so the hit flash (white) still reads against it.
 6. The window between the end of Telegraph and the strike is the Attack clip. Attack frame 2 is the hit-active frame unless a unit section says otherwise (Zed uses the same one-frame rule). The final Attack frame is a recovery pose that is clearly different from Idle (open, off balance), so the player sees the punish window.
- Super armour or guard states (Breaker Body Check dash, Calder Hydraulic Grab startup, Varr Command Shield, Copper Fang shield) are shown by a bright outline `#BFF4FF` drawn by the FX layer at runtime. Art must leave a clean outer silhouette for that outline to hug. FX owner to confirm (open question 6).
- Hit clip (2 frames): frame 1 snaps the head back and tilts the torso away; frame 2 holds the stagger. Heavy units flinch less: the Breaker and Calder Hit clips are 2 frames with a small shift only (they are unflinching during wind-ups; the engine simply does not play Hit then).

chunks.heading: 1.6 KO, tone
chunks.text: See section 3.2. Short form: KO is a knockdown. Held last frame is the lying pose; the game fades or removes the body.

chunks.heading: 1.7 Derived exports (no new drawing)
chunks.text:
Flag `d` in the counts below = a script or palette swap of already-drawn frames:
- `P2_` palette-swap exports for bosses whose phase 2 is a recolour/glow (Voss, Calder, Wren, Drone).
- `Idle_Cloak` and `Walk_Cloak` (Wren): outline-only variant of Idle/Walk, fill removed, 2 px outline `#4FB3D9`.
- Hologram `Idle` and `Walk`: Voss Idle and Walk re-exported flat Visor Cyan at 45 percent alpha with horizontal scanlines.
Each export script must be committed with the art so a later change to the base frames can be re-exported.
