No rule reconciles them, such as time bonuses, timer pauses, time added per kill or a fail state. The timer length, what happens at zero, and whether time pressure scales with difficulty are all missing. The "Fast-paced" tagline does not settle this either.
**Source:** "Defeat Wave / Clear Arena to win the level in time frame", the Timer Agent row, and "Defensive tools (block dodge, parry)".

chunks.heading: Finding 4: Combat and economy numbers are absent, so balance cannot be reasoned about (MAJOR)
chunks.text:
**Problem:** There are no damage values, health pools, hit or block stun frames, parry windows, combo scaling or juggle limits. There is nothing on pick-up objects: what they are, whether they are finite, and whether they are stronger than light and heavy attacks. "Enemies spawn to fight" gives no spawn rate, wave size, cap or escalation, so the difficulty curve cannot be inferred. There is also no health, lives, checkpoint or fail-state model. Parry and dodge cannot be balanced against enemy aggression without any of this.
**Source:** "light and heavy pick-up objects" (the sentence is garbled, so the intent is unclear), "Enemies spawn to fight", and the lack of any health or damage model anywhere in the document.

chunks.heading: Finding 5: The only numbers given are development token costs, not game systems (MINOR)
chunks.text:
**Problem:** The Technical Strategy budgets (200 tokens each for player movement and combos, Phaser "yet Unknown") describe build cost, not player-facing economy. Nothing links the "Agent" list to gameplay rules. For example, the Enemy Agent "will control the Enemies" and the Game Loop Agent "control the levels and win condition", but neither states what parameters it owns, so the design cannot be checked for whether the pieces interlock. The Player Mechanics row says only "Make the player move jump". There is no agent or spec for pickups, health or progression, so the systems the pitch highlights have no owner.
**Source:** The AI Architecture Team table and the Technical Strategy budget table.

chunks.heading: 1. CONFLICTS
chunks.text: **Business Analyst F3 (defensive kit is "decorative-risk scope", cut candidate) vs. my F3.** The analyst treats block/dodge/parry/juggle as optional extras to trim. I disagree. The timer/defense tension I raised is only a tension if defense is load-bearing. The document names "Defensive tools" as a core mechanic beside "Impactful Combat", and Enemy Agent behavior and the timer are the only pressure the player faces. If you cut defense, the loop becomes "hit things before the clock ends", and the timer then rewards nothing but raw DPS. So cutting is not free. It changes the design. The analyst is right that no MVP line exists, but the fix is to decide which systems the loop depends on first (my F1). Cost triage cannot substitute for that decision.

chunks.heading: 1. CONFLICTS
chunks.text:
**Player Psychologist F2 (timer harms learners; fix by tuning and feedback) vs. my F3.** We agree on the symptom but I think the psychologist frames it as a tuning problem. It is a structural one. A single timer number cannot serve both a first-time player learning parry and an expert running juggle routes. The document has no mechanism (time added per kill, timer pause on parry, per-difficulty scaling) that would make one value work. So "tune it" has nothing to tune with. I would keep my MAJOR rating and reject "add feedback" as sufficient.
**Adversarial QA F1 (two contradictory win conditions) vs. my F3.** QA reads "Defeat Wave / Clear Arena ... in time frame" as possibly meaning "survive until the timer ends". I built F3 on the reading that the clock is a deadline. QA's ambiguity is fair, and it means my F3 rests on an unstated assumption. Under a survive-the-timer reading, the defense/timer conflict largely disappears, since turtling becomes the correct play. Either reading breaks a different part of the design, which strengthens the case that this must be specified.

chunks.heading: 2. CONNECTIONS
chunks.text: **QA F2 (spawn rules) + my F4 (no numbers) = the difficulty curve has no control variable.** QA shows that time-driven versus clear-driven spawning produces opposite failure modes (unbounded accumulation versus edge exploits). I flagged missing spawn rate and caps. Combined, the point is that spawn logic is the only lever this design has for difficulty, because there are no enemy types and no progression. Since the Enemy Agent owns behavior and the Game Loop Agent owns the win condition, and neither is budgeted (QA F5), the one lever that sets difficulty has no owner and no cost. Neither of us saw that alone.

chunks.heading: 2. CONNECTIONS
chunks.text:
**Player Psychologist F1 (no onboarding) + my F2 (no progression) = there is no unlock order to teach through.** The psychologist wants sequenced teaching of moves. A sequence needs a progression system that gates tools over time. The document has neither, so all of light, heavy, combos, juggle, block, dodge and parry are available in level one. That is a systems problem, not just a UX one. Without gating, level one and the last level have the same toolset, which also removes the only means of pacing the difficulty.
**Feasibility F3 (Combos and Mechanics agents share the animation constraint) + my F1.** The Player Combos Agent is described only as "Take care of the players combos with the game". Feasibility notes the coupling on the build side. On the design side it means combos, defense and cancels are one state machine, which is exactly what my F3 says cannot be reasoned about separately. Splitting them into two 200-token agents hides the interaction that decides whether timer pressure and defense can coexist.

chunks.heading: 2. CONNECTIONS
chunks.text: **Narrative Critic F3 (no fiction reason for the clock) + my F3.** A diegetic timer (reinforcements arriving) would give a natural rule for the tension I flagged. For example, the time limit could be the arrival of extra enemies. That doubles as a difficulty-scaling mechanism and a fail-state, and solves a systems gap and a story gap with one rule. This is the kind of cross-lens fix that neither review proposes alone.

chunks.heading: 3. REVISIONS
chunks.text:
- **F3: keep MAJOR, but state its dependency.** I now say explicitly that it depends on the timer being a deadline, per QA F1. I would add that the spec must first choose between deadline and survive-until semantics.
- **F4: upgrade from MAJOR toward BLOCKING-adjacent for the fail-state portion.** QA F1 and the psychologist F4 both independently note there is no death, lives or timeout rule. A loop with no lose condition is not a loop. I had folded the fail state into F4 as a sub-point. I would split it out and raise it to BLOCKING, merged with F1, since a loop needs a lose branch as much as a reward branch.
- **F5: downgrade acknowledged and narrowed.** The Business Analyst F5 and Feasibility F3 cover the agent/budget mismatch better than I did. I withdraw the token-cost commentary as a systems concern. I keep only the point that progression, health and pickups have no owner, because that is a gap in design ownership rather than a build-cost issue.
- **F2: unchanged (BLOCKING),** now corroborated by four other reviewers (narrative F5, psychologist F3, business F2, QA F4) without contradiction. I would hold that any resolution should decide whether progression is in scope at all. The business analyst's "tech demo versus shippable game" framing is a valid way to resolve it, and dropping the promise is an acceptable answer.

chunks.heading: Visualization Audit: review-viz.html
chunks.text:
Scope: `review-viz.html` (embedded `DATA`), `reviews/viz-data.json`, the six reviewer files, and `SYNTHESIS.md`.
Method: read-only. I did not run the page. I read the JavaScript for syntax errors, undefined names, TDZ problems and wrong JSON keys. Layout and overlap comments are inferred from the CSS and the coordinate math, so treat them as unverified.

chunks.heading: Visualization Audit: review-viz.html
chunks.text:
Baseline checks that passed:
- The embedded `DATA` matches `viz-data.json` on every block I compared: meta, aggregate counts, findings, conflicts, connections, revisions, top issues, disagreements, quick wins and verdict. This was a visual comparison, not a mechanical diff.
- The 30 findings (6 reviewers x 5) each match their reviewer file on title, Round 1 severity and post-Round-2 severity.
- Round 1 severity counts are 8 BLOCKING, 16 MAJOR, 6 MINOR, which matches the source.
- Final counts are 9 BLOCKING, 18 MAJOR, 2 MINOR, 1 WITHDRAWN. This holds under the "split counts once at highest severity" rule.
- Conflict counts per reviewer (3/3/4/5/3/4 = 22) and connection counts per reviewer (4/5/5/5/4/5 = 28) match the Round 2 sections of the reviewer files.
- The five top issues, their severities and outcomes, the four disagreements with every position and attribution, the three quick wins with `suggested_by`, and the verdict and Tier 0 slice all match `SYNTHESIS.md`.
- The JavaScript key names match the JSON (`severity_round1`, `severity_final`, `flagged_by`, `reviewers_combined`, and so on). I found no syntax errors and no undefined variables.
 - `r1?.2:1` parses as a ternary, not optional chaining.
 - The `nm` shadowing in `renderV2` does not cause a TDZ error.
 - Function declarations used before their definition are hoisted.

chunks.heading: 1. Accuracy errors
chunks.text:
1. **Issue 2 reviewer count is wrong (section 5, accordion header).**
 - HTML: "5 reviewers". The code prints `it.refs.length`.
 - Source: Issue 2's `flagged_by` has 5 entries, but Technical Feasibility Lead appears twice (F1, and F4 as corroboration). That is 4 distinct reviewers: Feasibility, Business Analyst, QA and Systems Designer.
 - The other issues are correct: 6, 5, 4 and 4.
 - Fix: count `new Set(refs.map(r=>r.code)).size`.

chunks.heading: 1. Accuracy errors
chunks.text:
2. **Finding-level "cross-exam outcome" labels are not in the source and are applied inconsistently.**
 - Sections 2 and 6 and the Status filter give every finding SURVIVED, STRENGTHENED, WEAKENED, SPLIT or WITHDRAWN. `SYNTHESIS.md` uses those words only for the five top issues. The page derives the finding-level labels itself. The footer discloses this, but only at the bottom of the page.
 - The derivation contradicts the source in these cases:
 - **Systems Designer F1** shows SURVIVED beside the revision tag UPGRADED and the detail "Merged with fail-state portion; remains BLOCKING".
 - **Feasibility F4** shows WEAKENED, but its severity goes MAJOR to MAJOR. The source says only that a proposed BLOCKING was reverted; it was never a Round 1 rating.
 - **Systems F5, Narrative F5 and QA F4** show WEAKENED with no severity change. Systems F5 goes MINOR to MINOR, Narrative F5 goes MINOR to MINOR, and QA F4 goes MAJOR to MAJOR. Their downgrade is the narrowing of the finding, not its rating. The Sankey draws MAJOR to WEAKENED to MAJOR, and the reader sees no reason for it.
 - **QA F5** is a genuine split ("MAJOR (ownership gap) / MINOR (rest)") but is labelled STRENGTHENED. **QA F3** is labelled SPLIT although its severity did not change. So SPLIT is applied to one split finding and one non-split, while the true severity split (QA F5) is missed.
 - The same words mean different things at issue level and finding level.
 - Issue 3 is WEAKENED in the synthesis, yet its Systems F1 and F2 rows show BLOCKING to BLOCKING and SURVIVED.
 - Issue 2 is SURVIVED, yet its card contains Feasibility F4 (WEAKENED), Systems F5 (WEAKENED) and QA F5 (STRENGTHENED).
 - Fix options: rename the finding-level labels (for example "Severity raised / lowered / unchanged / split / withdrawn"), or drop them and use the Round 2 revision types. Keep the synthesis words for issues only.

chunks.heading: 1. Accuracy errors
chunks.text:
3. **A revision type appears that the reviewer never stated.**
 - `viz-data.json` and the HTML list Systems Designer F1 as `UPGRADED`. `systems-designer.md` Round 2 revises only F3, F4, F5 and F2. F1 is mentioned only as the item F4's fail-state portion is merged into.
 - The V6 detail row shows "Round 2 revision: UPGRADED" for a finding rated BLOCKING throughout. This is a data-file error that the page repeats.
4. **The "(most)" marker on the disagreement grid is misleading.**
 - Disagreements A and C both have 4 distinct positions, but only the first row (A) gets "(most)" and the heavy left border. C has the same number.
 - Suggest tagging every tied row, or dropping the tag.
5. **Minor wording mismatch.**
 - Disagreement D's escalated decision reads "Escalated: Not settled. Feasibility conceded ..." That is the synthesis text. It is accurate but reads as an escalation to nobody.

chunks.heading: 1. Accuracy errors
chunks.text: No missing, duplicated or invented findings were found. No reviewer attribution errors were found. Disagreement positions are attributed to the right reviewers, and the shared-position grouping (Feasibility + Business Analyst in A and C, Player Psychologist + Feasibility in B) matches the synthesis. The top-issue cards link the right F-IDs.

chunks.heading: MUST-FIX
chunks.text:
- **The status vocabulary is not explained where it is used.**
 - Sankey column 2 ("CROSS-EXAM OUTCOME"), the Status filter chips, the V5 status pills and the V6 Status column all show words with no definition nearby. The only definition is in the page footer.
 - As explained in accuracy error 2, the words are also inconsistent with the synthesis. A first-time reader will read "WEAKENED" as "the reviewers doubted this finding", which is not what it means here.
 - Fix: add a one-line definition under the V2 subtitle and a tooltip on the Status chips, and rename the labels (see accuracy error 2).

chunks.heading: SHOULD-FIX
chunks.text:
- **The Round control is confusing and partly inert.**
 - "Round" (Round 1 / After cross-exam / Both) only changes section 1's bars and section 3's network. It does nothing to sections 2, 4, 5 or 6.
 - "Use Round 1 severity" is a second, overlapping control that changes what the Severity chips and table filter against.
 - The two together are hard to reason about. Choosing "Round 1" also fades the network to 20% with "No cross-examination in Round 1", which looks like a broken chart.
 - Fix: fold both into one "Severity basis" control. Do not tie the network to it.
- **Clicking a section 1 bar has a hidden, large side effect.**
 - `segClick` changes the Reviewer, Severity, Round and basis filters together. Clicking a Round 1 bar also sets Round to Round 1, which fades the section 3 network. Nothing in the section 1 subtitle says the bars are clickable.
 - The result is only visible as dimming and a small "n of 30 findings match" in the sticky bar. There is no visible "selected" state on the bar itself.
 - Fix: say "Click a bar to filter" in the subtitle, and do not set Round.

chunks.heading: SHOULD-FIX
chunks.text:
- **The sticky filter bar is tall.**
 - It carries six reviewer chips, four severity chips, a basis chip, a round control, five status chips, Reset and a counter. At typical laptop widths that is 3 to 4 rows, roughly 130 to 170px of every screen.
 - `section.viz` uses `scroll-margin-top:110px`, so section headings can land under the bar.
 - Fix: collapse the Status group behind a "More filters" toggle, or make the bar non-sticky.
- **Network pins are inconsistent.**
 - Clicking an edge pins it and also filters the whole page to that pair (`S.rev`). Clicking a node pins it and does not filter.
 - The panel text says "Click pins the selection and filters to that pair", which is only true for edges.
 - A pair with both a conflict and a connection draws two lines. Clicking the second line of the pair un-pins instead of switching to it, because the pin key is the pair.

chunks.heading: SHOULD-FIX
chunks.text:
- **Network panel content disappears on hover-out.**
 - Hover fills the panel, and leaving the chart resets it to the intro text. The panel has `max-height:520px; overflow:auto`, so you cannot scroll long content without pinning first.
 - The intro text mentions pinning, but the mismatch will surprise people.
- **The node panel omits connections.**
 - It states "found N connections" but lists only conflicts raised and revisions. It also lists only conflicts the node raised, while the highlighted edges include conflicts against the node.
- **Section 1 label crowding (unverified).**
 - The "Round 1" and "Final" labels are right-aligned at x=162, and the row label is left-aligned at x=0 with a 13px mono font.
 - "PSY Psychologist" (16 characters) and "FEA Feasibility" (15) run to roughly x=117 to 125, and "Round 1" spans roughly x=102 to 162. Vertical spacing is about 1px, so labels may touch or overlap.
 - Render it and check.

chunks.heading: SHOULD-FIX
chunks.text:
- **Duplicate `id="v6"`.**
 - Both `<section id="v6">` (line 227) and `<table id="v6">` (line 233) use it.
 - The page still works because the selectors use descendant matching (`#v6 thead`, `#v6 tbody`). But `$('#v6').addEventListener(...)` binds to the section, and the `scrollIntoView` fallback scrolls to the section.
 - It is invalid HTML and an accessibility risk. Rename the table (for example `v6table`) and update the selectors.
- **Hover on a V6 row highlights charts that are off-screen.**
 - `xhl` dims the section 1 rows, section 3 nodes and section 4 headers, and highlights the Sankey ribbons. They are all above the table and out of view. The effect is invisible in practice.

chunks.heading: NICE-TO-FIX
chunks.text:
- The V3 node radius (16 + 1.3 x items) ranges only from about 32px to 36px, because items authored range from 12 to 15. "Node size is items authored" is not readable.
- A gap between about 900 and 1050px viewport width may clip the "Psychologist" label in the network (the chart card is about 540px wide). It scrolls horizontally in `.scrollx`.
- With both Conflicts and Connections toggled off, the network shows nothing and no message.
- Hover highlight in the network sticks when the pointer moves onto empty SVG space. It clears only when leaving the whole chart.
- `.hv` and `.hovering` classes: `.hv` has no CSS (harmless).
- The footer says "Built from viz-data.json", but the data is a copy embedded in the HTML. Editing the JSON will not change the page.
- The header stats show BLOCKING 8 to 9 and MINOR 6 to 2 but not MAJOR (16 to 18) or the 1 withdrawn, so the four numbers do not visibly sum.
- V4 says "No position recorded" for reviewers with no stated position. That reads as an abstention. "Not stated in synthesis" is more accurate.
- There is no in-page navigation. The skip link goes to `#v1` only. Six long sections and no table of contents.
- The default sort in V6 (final severity, then issue) is sensible, but the "ID" sort orders alphabetically by reviewer code (BIZ first), which is not the reviewers' order used elsewhere.

chunks.heading: What works well
chunks.text:
- Every chart has a "View as table" fallback. The empty-state messages have working Reset buttons.
- Filter chips use check and cross marks plus dashed borders (not color alone).
- The top-5 accordion, the finding table with search and sort, CSV export, keyboard access and focus management are solid.
- Disagreement cells show a position tag and expand for the full argument.
- The verdict block is at the top, with the Tier 0 slice.

chunks.heading: 3. Verdict
chunks.text:
**Needs another pass. Not ready to show yet.**
The data layer is sound. Counts, severities, attributions, disagreement positions and quick wins all trace to the source files, and I found no JavaScript that should fail on load. There is one hard factual error (Issue 2 shows "5 reviewers" for 4) and one data error carried through (Systems F1 tagged UPGRADED).
The main problem is the derived finding-level status labels. They reuse the synthesis vocabulary with a different meaning, are applied inconsistently, and are explained only in the footer. Fix those, then fix the Round and basis controls and the section 1 click side effect, and the page will be ready. The rest are polish.
Recommended order:
1. Fix the Issue 2 count.
2. Rename and explain the status labels.
3. Correct Systems F1's revision type in the JSON and the HTML.
4. Simplify Round and basis.
5. Rename the duplicate `v6` id.
6. Load the page once in a browser to check the section 1 label overlap and the network at about 1000px width.

chunks.heading: 0. Read this first: data source caveat
chunks.text: `reviews/viz-data.json` does not exist at the path given (read returned "File does not exist"). This spec is therefore built from the six reviewer files and `SYNTHESIS.md`. Section 8 defines the JSON shape the visualizations need. If `viz-data.json` is generated later, map its fields to that shape. Every number below was hand-counted from the review files, so it can be used as a test fixture.

chunks.heading: 1. Page layout (top to bottom, single scrolling page, max width 1200px)
chunks.text:
| Order | Block | Height | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Header + verdict strip | 120px | One-sentence verdict from SYNTHESIS section 4, plus 4 count chips (30 findings, 6 reviewers, 8 to 12 BLOCKING, 4 open disagreements) |
| 0 | Global filter bar (sticky) | 56px | Drives every viz below. See section 2 |
| 1 | V1 Severity shift | 320px | Full width |
| 2 | V2 Finding flow (Sankey) | 460px | Full width |
| 3 | V3 Cross-exam network | 520px | 60% width, with a 40% detail panel to its right |
| 4 | V4 Disagreement matrix | 340px | Full width |
| 5 | V5 Top 5 issues drill-down | 5 cards, ~110px collapsed | Full width |
| 6 | V6 Findings table | 480px, scrolls | Full width, the "everything else" view |
Order is deliberate: overview (V1), what changed (V2), who did it (V3), where they still clash (V4), what to fix (V5), raw lookup (V6).

chunks.heading: 2. Global filter bar (state shared by all viz)
chunks.text:
Controls:
- Reviewer: multi-select chips (Systems, Narrative, Psychologist, Feasibility, QA, Business). Default all.
- Severity: BLOCKING / MAJOR / MINOR toggles. Applies to the **final** severity by default; a small switch "Use Round 1 severity" changes the basis.
- Round: segmented control `Round 1 | After cross-exam | Both`. Default Both.
- Status: Survived / Strengthened / Weakened / Split / Withdrawn (multi).
- Reset link.
Behavior: any change re-renders all viz within 150ms. Items outside the filter are dimmed to 15% opacity, not removed, in V1 to V4, so layout does not jump. V5 and V6 remove non-matching rows. The filter state is mirrored in the URL hash so a view can be shared. Clicking a mark in any viz sets the corresponding filter (click again to clear), except where noted.
Color system (use everywhere): BLOCKING = red #C0392B, MAJOR = amber #E6A23C, MINOR = grey-blue #7F8FA6, WITHDRAWN = light grey with dashed outline. Reviewers get a fixed categorical palette of 6 colors distinct from the severity colors (use shapes or initials as a second cue, for color-blind users).

chunks.heading: 3. V1: Severity shift (stacked bars, Round 1 vs final)
chunks.text:
**Shows:** how the 30 findings distribute across severities, per reviewer and overall, and how much cross-examination moved them. This is the "big picture first" chart.
**Chart type:** Horizontal stacked bars. 7 rows: "All reviewers" (top, taller, separated by a rule) then the 6 reviewers. Each row holds a **pair** of thin bars: upper = Round 1, lower = Final (post cross-exam). Segments colored by severity, with the count printed inside a segment if the segment is wide enough.
**Data:** `findings[].reviewer`, `findings[].severity_r1`, `findings[].severity_final`, `findings[].status`. Withdrawn findings appear as a fourth hatched grey segment in the Final bar so totals stay comparable.
**Expected values for verification (Round 1):** BLOCKING 8, MAJOR 16, MINOR 6 = 30. Per reviewer: Systems 2/2/1, Narrative 2/2/1, Psychologist 1/3/1, Feasibility 1/3/1, QA 1/3/1, Business 1/3/1. Final values depend on the split rule in section 8 (a split finding counts as 2 items).

chunks.heading: 3. V1: Severity shift (stacked bars, Round 1 vs final)
chunks.text:
**Interaction:**
- Hover a segment: tooltip "Feasibility, Round 1: 3 MAJOR" plus a list of the finding titles in it (max 5, then "+n more").
- Click a segment: sets Reviewer + Severity + Round filters.
- Hover between the two bars of one row: a thin connector shows net movement, e.g. "+1 BLOCKING, -1 MINOR".
- Legend doubles as the severity filter.
**Size/position:** full width, 320px. Left label column 140px.
**Why it is informative and not decorative:** it shows that BLOCKING grew and MINOR shrank after cross-examination, which is the first evidence that the multi-agent process changed the outcome.

chunks.heading: 4. V2: Finding flow (Sankey)
chunks.text:
**Shows:** how findings changed from Round 1 through cross-examination to the final synthesis.
**Chart type:** 3-column Sankey.
- Column 1, "Round 1 severity": BLOCKING, MAJOR, MINOR (node heights = counts, 8/16/6).
- Column 2, "Cross-exam outcome": Survived unchanged, Strengthened (raised), Weakened (lowered), Split (part raised, part kept), Withdrawn or folded into another finding.
- Column 3, "Final severity": BLOCKING, MAJOR, MINOR, Withdrawn.
- Ribbon color = Round 1 severity. Ribbon opacity 0.55, full on hover.

chunks.heading: 4. V2: Finding flow (Sankey)
chunks.text:
**Data:** `findings[].severity_r1`, `.status`, `.severity_final`. Items known from the files to place:
- Strengthened: Feasibility F5 (MINOR to MAJOR), Psychologist F5 (MINOR to MAJOR), QA F5 (MINOR to MAJOR, ownership gap only), Narrative F2 stays BLOCKING but narrowed (count as Survived, narrowed).
- Weakened: Narrative F1 (BLOCKING to MAJOR), Narrative F5 (MINOR to a note).
- Split: Systems F4 (fail state raised to BLOCKING, merged with F1), Psychologist F4 (fail-and-retry BLOCKING, rest MAJOR), QA F3 (split).
- Withdrawn or folded: Business F5 (withdrawn), Systems F5 (token commentary withdrawn, ownership point kept).
- Survived: the remainder.
Use the `status` field from the data as the source of truth; the list above is a check.

chunks.heading: 4. V2: Finding flow (Sankey)
chunks.text:
**Interaction:**
- Hover a ribbon: highlights the ribbon and shows a card "Feasibility F5: 'Success criteria vague' MINOR to MAJOR. Reason: Business Analyst F3 showed the missing must-have set is how scope explodes." (text from `change_reason`).
- Hover a node: highlights all ribbons through it and shows its count.
- Click a ribbon or node: sets filters and scrolls V6 to the matching rows, expanding the first.
- Click a Column 2 label: toggles that status in the global Status filter.
**Size/position:** full width, 460px, node width 18px, column gap wide enough for ribbon labels.
**Note:** if the developer only has time to build one of V1 and V2 well, keep V2. V1 stays because it is the only per-reviewer breakdown and it is cheap.

chunks.heading: 5. V3: Cross-examination network
chunks.text:
**Shows:** who engaged with whom in Round 2, and what kind of link they made. This is the multi-agent payoff.
**Chart type:** Node-link diagram with 6 fixed nodes placed on a hexagon (deterministic layout, no physics, so it does not jitter). Edges are curved arcs between reviewers. Node size = number of Round 2 items authored (conflicts + connections + revisions). Edge thickness = number of items linking the pair. Edges are undirected by default; a "Direction" toggle draws arrowheads from author to target.

chunks.heading: 5. V3: Cross-examination network
chunks.text:
**Edge types (toggle chips above the chart, all on by default):**
- CONFLICT (solid red): a reviewer disputes another reviewer's finding. Examples from the files: Systems vs Business on defense, Psychologist vs Feasibility on onboarding severity, QA vs Psychologist on timer.
- CONNECTION (solid teal): two reviewers' findings combine into a new insight neither had alone. Examples: QA F2 + Systems F4 (spawn is the only difficulty lever), Feasibility + Systems (health/hitbox has no owner).
- CONCESSION (dashed blue): a reviewer accepts another's point and revises. Examples: Feasibility concedes the QA trio is a bigger hole, Narrative concedes to Feasibility and Business on severity.
**Data:** `crossexam[]` items with `from`, `to`, `type`, `summary`, `target_finding_ids`, and `connection_insight` (for CONNECTION type). Round 2 counts per reviewer: each reviewer wrote a CONFLICTS, CONNECTIONS, and REVISIONS section.

chunks.heading: 5. V3: Cross-examination network
chunks.text:
**Interaction:**
- Hover an edge: highlights it, dims others, and fills the right-hand detail panel with each exchange as a mini card (type badge, one-line summary, the two finding IDs).
- Hover a node: highlights all edges of that reviewer; panel shows their stance summary (findings raised, findings revised).
- Click an edge: pins the detail panel and sets the Reviewer filter to the pair.
- Click a mini card's finding ID: scrolls to the matching row in V6 and expands it.
- Filters: dims nodes and edges for reviewers not selected; the Round filter set to "Round 1" shows an empty-state message "No cross-examination in Round 1" and greys the chart.
**Size/position:** 60% width (about 700px) x 520px for the chart; the 40% detail panel scrolls independently. Below 900px viewport width, the panel moves below the chart.
**Headline callout above the chart (computed):** "Most connected pair: X and Y (n links)", and "Most contested pair: X and Y (n conflicts)".

chunks.heading: 6. V4: Disagreement matrix (stance heatmap)
chunks.text:
**Shows:** where reviewers still clash after cross-examination. This is deliberately topic-based (unlike V3, which is pair-based), so the two do not duplicate.
**Chart type:** Heatmap grid. Rows = the 4 unresolved disagreements from SYNTHESIS section 2:
- A. Do progression, onboarding and story block the prototype?
- B. Is the defensive kit (block, dodge, parry) cuttable?
- C. How should the timer be specified?
- D. Where does the main integration risk sit?
Columns = the 6 reviewers. Each cell shows that reviewer's **stance** as a short label plus a color from a diverging scale: e.g. for A, "Blocks" (dark red) to "Post-prototype" (blue); for B, "Load-bearing" vs "Cut first" vs "Tiered". A cell is empty (hatched) if the reviewer took no position.
**Data:** `disagreements[]` with `id`, `question`, `stances[]` of `{reviewer, position_label, position_score (-1 to +1), quote}`. The initial stances are in SYNTHESIS section 2 and the Round 2 sections of each review.

chunks.heading: 6. V4: Disagreement matrix (stance heatmap)
chunks.text:
**Row summary:** on the right of each row, a "spread" badge: `spread = max(score) - min(score)`. Rows are sorted by spread descending, with the top row outlined in red as the "active clash". Also show the moderator's escalation question in italics under the row title.
**Interaction:**
- Hover a cell: tooltip with the reviewer's quote (max 200 chars) and the finding IDs it refers to.
- Click a cell: expands a panel under the row with the reviewer's full argument, and highlights the opposing cells (score difference >= 1) with a red border.
- Click a row title: sets V6 to the findings linked to that disagreement (`disagreements[].finding_ids`).
- Global Reviewer filter dims columns.
**Size/position:** full width, about 340px. Cells min 150x64px.
**Note:** an earlier idea was a generic reviewer-by-reviewer agree/disagree grid. It was dropped because with 6 reviewers and 4 topics, the topic-by-stance grid says more, and V3 already shows pairs.

chunks.heading: 7. V5: Top 5 issues drill-down (expandable cards)
chunks.text:
**Shows:** the five ranked issues from SYNTHESIS section 1, each with its full trail.
**Chart type:** Vertical list of 5 expandable cards (accordion, multiple open allowed).
**Collapsed card (about 110px):** rank number, title, severity badge (final), status badge (STRENGTHENED / SURVIVED / WEAKENED), and a mini "trail bar": one dot per flagging reviewer colored by reviewer, plus a tiny R1-to-final severity arrow (e.g. MAJOR to BLOCKING). Right edge: "n reviewers".
The 5 cards, in order:
1. No lose condition (BLOCKING, STRENGTHENED). Flagged by all 6.
2. No production plan (BLOCKING, SURVIVED). Feasibility F1, Business F1, plus QA/Systems corroboration.
3. Progression and level structure undefined (BLOCKING/MAJOR, WEAKENED).
4. Spawn, enemy behavior, health/damage/hitbox ownership (MAJOR, STRENGTHENED).
5. Timer undefined and pulls against defensive depth (MAJOR, STRENGTHENED).

chunks.heading: 7. V5: Top 5 issues drill-down (expandable cards)
chunks.text:
**Expanded card, three stacked sections (a timeline):**
1. **Original findings (Round 1):** one row per contributing finding: reviewer chip, finding ID, title, R1 severity, and a 1-2 sentence excerpt of "Problem" plus the "Source" quote in a quoted block.
2. **Cross-examination:** a chronological list of Round 2 items touching this issue: type badge (CONFLICT / CONNECTION / REVISION), author to target, one-line argument. Severity changes are shown inline as "MAJOR to BLOCKING".
3. **Final status:** severity, status, moderator outcome text from SYNTHESIS, the escalated decision if any (linked to the V4 row), and the quick win that closes it (SYNTHESIS section 3) if one exists.
**Data:** `top_issues[]` with `rank`, `title`, `severity_final`, `status`, `finding_ids[]`, `outcome_text`, `quick_win_id`. Trail items are joined from `findings[]` and `crossexam[]` by `finding_ids`.

chunks.heading: 7. V5: Top 5 issues drill-down (expandable cards)
chunks.text:
**Interaction:**
- Click card header: expand or collapse. Keyboard: Enter/Space, arrows to move between cards.
- Hover a reviewer dot in the collapsed trail bar: tooltip with reviewer and finding ID.
- Click a reviewer chip inside an expanded card: sets the Reviewer filter.
- "Expand all / Collapse all" link top right.
- Cards are not removed by filters (they are the synthesis); instead reviewers outside the filter are dimmed inside the trail.
- Deep link: `#issue-1` opens card 1.
**Size/position:** full width, list. Expanded card grows to fit; the text column max width 760px for readability.

chunks.heading: 8. V6: Findings table (filter and sort)
chunks.text:
**Shows:** all 30 findings (32 rows if splits are counted as two) for lookup, filtering and sorting. This is where the global filters are most visible.
**Chart type:** Sortable table with a sticky header.
**Columns:** ID (e.g. FEAS-F1), Reviewer (chip), Title, Round 1 severity, Final severity, Change (arrow, or "=" ), Status badge, # colleagues who referenced it, Top issue # (if any).
**Sorting:** click a header to sort; shift-click for secondary sort. Default sort: Final severity (BLOCKING first), then # references descending. Severity sorts by rank, not alphabetically.
**Interaction:**
- Row click: expands inline to show the Problem, Source quote, and the Round 2 items that reference it (same content as V5 section 2, shorter).
- Text search box above the table (filters on title and problem text).
- Filter chips in the global bar apply; a result count "Showing 12 of 30" is displayed above the table.
- Row hover: highlights the same finding's ribbon in V2 and its reviewer's node in V3 (cross-highlighting).
- Export CSV of the current view (button top right).

chunks.heading: 8. V6: Findings table (filter and sort)
chunks.text: **Size/position:** full width, 480px viewport with internal scroll; on mobile, columns collapse to ID, Title, Final severity.

chunks.heading: 9. Data contract (what each viz reads)
chunks.text:
If `viz-data.json` is produced, it needs these arrays. Field names below are the ones this spec uses; rename in one adapter file if the real file differs.
```
findings[] id, reviewer, title, problem, source_quote, severity_r1,
 severity_final, status (survived|strengthened|weakened|split|withdrawn),
 change_reason, merged_into (id or null), referenced_by[]
crossexam[] id, from, to, type (conflict|connection|concession),
 summary, target_finding_ids[], connection_insight
disagreements[] id (A-D), question, escalation, finding_ids[],
 stances[{reviewer, position_label, position_score, quote}]
top_issues[] rank, title, severity_final, status, finding_ids[],
 outcome_text, quick_win_id
quick_wins[] id, title, closes_issue_ranks[]
```

chunks.heading: 9. Data contract (what each viz reads)
chunks.text:
Rules for the adapter:
- A split finding produces two rows in `findings` that share a parent id (`SYS-F4a`, `SYS-F4b`), each with its own severity. Counts in V1 and V2 use rows, so totals may exceed 30; the V1 header should say "30 original findings, n after splits".
- `merged_into` finding rows are counted in V2 as "Withdrawn or folded".
- Hover cross-highlighting requires every row, ribbon and node to carry a `data-finding-id` or `data-reviewer` attribute.

chunks.heading: 10. Cut list (considered and dropped)
chunks.text:
- Standalone reviewer-vs-reviewer agreement matrix: replaced by V4 (topic-based) plus V3 (pair-based). Three views of the same insight would be redundant.
- Separate "sort and filter" panel: folded into the global bar and V6.
- Word cloud, radar chart of reviewer "personality", timeline animation of rounds: decorative, no decision value.
- Quick wins as a standalone viz: only 3 items; shown as a footer of each V5 card instead.

chunks.heading: 11. Accessibility and build notes
chunks.text:
- All charts must have a text equivalent: V1 and V2 provide a "View as table" toggle showing the underlying counts.
- Color is never the only cue: severity badges carry text, network edges differ in dash pattern, reviewers carry initials.
- Suggested libraries: d3 with d3-sankey for V2; plain SVG or d3 for V1, V3, V4; native `<details>`-style accordions for V5; no framework is required.
- Performance is not a concern (about 30 findings and about 60 cross-exam items).
- Empty states: if a filter yields zero items, each viz shows "No findings match these filters" with a Reset link, not a blank canvas.

chunks.heading: Playtest agents (goal-oriented, adversarial, recorded)
chunks.text:
Two blackboard agents that **play** The Rebellion and record it:
| Goal | Agent | Plays | Publishes |
|---|---|---|---|
| G7 | `playtest-level-agent` | levels 1-8 start to finish (Brawler) + adversarial passes | `blackboard/facts/playtest-levels.json` |
| G8 | `playtest-boss-agent` | mini-bosses and end-of-level bosses (Boss Hunter) + adversarial passes | `blackboard/facts/playtest-bosses.json` |
Both need nothing upstream, so the director can run them in parallel with G1/G2, or after G6 to check a generated change.

chunks.heading: Watch one now
chunks.text:
```
python dev-server.py 8777
http://localhost:8777/playtest.html?level=1&agent=brawler
http://localhost:8777/playtest.html?level=1&wave=5&agent=boss-hunter     (Brick Dugan)
```
The panel in the bottom-right corner shows the agent's current goal, action, hits, parries and live findings.
Drop `&agent=...` to play the level yourself without the title/menu.

chunks.heading: Record everything
chunks.text:
```
npm i -D playwright && npx playwright install chromium     (once)
node qa/playtest-agents/run.mjs --suite levels             (or bosses, or all)
node qa/playtest-agents/run.mjs --only L1-brawler,EB-L1-dugan-crew --headed
```
Options: `--seed N` (replay the same run), `--renderer canvas` (no GPU / CI), `--out <dir>`, `--no-blackboard`.
Output goes to `qa/playtest-agents/runs/<stamp>/`: `videos/<run>.mp4` (webm if ffmpeg is missing), `REPORT.md`, `report.json`.

chunks.heading: Files
chunks.text:
- `agent.js`: the brain. perceive -> score goals -> act through real KeyboardEvents; `Monitor` checks invariants every step; `report()` returns stats, boss move read-out, findings and a timeline.
- `personas.js`: Brawler, Boss Hunter, Parry Master (competent); Button Masher, Edge Exploiter, Turtle (adversarial).
- `scenarios.js`: which level/wave each run plays.
- `run.mjs`: static server + Playwright recorder + reports + blackboard facts.
- `../../playtest.html`: boots straight into `?level=N` (and honours ArenaScene's `?wave=N`).
Game code is not touched. The agent only reads `ArenaScene` state and presses keys.

chunks.heading: Severity (same scale as qa-agent)
chunks.text: S1 blocks winning or losing (soft-lock, stuck grab, no result screen, NaN). S2 breaks a contract (bounds leak, frozen timer, enemy stuck off-screen, JS errors). S3 wrong but playable (scenario cap hit, balance outliers). S4 polish.

---
name: playtest-boss-agent
description: Goal-oriented adversarial playtester for The Rebellion's mini-bosses and end-of-level bosses. Records video of a Boss Hunter persona reading every boss tell (charge strip, Mega Stomp, grab reach, Rage Punch) plus adversarial passes, measures which moves land and which get evaded, and publishes findings to the blackboard (G8). Use after any boss change or to SEE a boss fight.
tools: Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep, Bash
---
You are the **Playtest Boss Agent** for *The Rebellion: Fists of the Fallen City*. You own blackboard goal **G8-playtest-bosses**. You play boss fights, record them and measure them; you do not fix game code.

chunks.heading: What you fight (`qa/playtest-agents/scenarios.js`, BOSS_SCENARIOS)
chunks.text:
- **Mini-bosses**: "Brick" Dugan (L1 W5, canon Level 1 mini-boss, the only bespoke boss AI today), Overseer Holt wave (L4 W2), Copper Fang wave (L5 W2), Overseer Wren wave (L5 W5).
- **End-of-level bosses**: Dugan + crew (Level 1 finale), Copper Fang (L5 W7, L7 W3), Overseer Halden Varr (L8 W4, final boss).
- **Adversarial**: Dugan vs Edge Exploiter (corner him: wall crashes, charge into walls) and vs Button Masher (input fuzz during grabs/stomps).
Boss waves other than Dugan are stand-in grunts with an HP multiplier (`levelData.js` STAND_IN). Report that as a gap, not as a pass.

chunks.heading: How you play
chunks.text: The `boss-hunter` persona in `qa/playtest-agents/agent.js` reads Dugan's state every frame: sidesteps in depth when the red charge strip shows, jumps when the Mega Stomp wave front is ~120 px away, back-steps a grab wind-up, mashes J/K when held, parries punches on the closing ring (one press per attack, like a player), uses K to break his block and punishes recovery. The monitor records, per boss move: times seen, times it hit Zed, times evaded, damage, plus time-to-KO.

chunks.heading: Run it
chunks.text:
1. `node blackboard/board.mjs claim G8-playtest-bosses playtest-boss-agent`.
2. `npm test` green first, else `block`.
3. `node qa/playtest-agents/run.mjs --suite bosses` (`--renderer canvas` without a GPU; `--only EB-L1-dugan-crew`; `--headed` to watch).
4. Read `REPORT.md` -> "Boss move read-out". Flag as balance findings (S3) any move a boss-hunter cannot evade more than half the time, any boss killed in under 15 s or not killed in 120 s, and any parry success rate under 30 percent (telegraph may be unreadable). Watch the video at the timestamp before filing.
5. The runner writes `blackboard/facts/playtest-bosses.json`; put new work in `requests`.
6. `node blackboard/board.mjs done G8-playtest-bosses "<cleared>/<fights>, S1:<n> S2:<n>"`.

chunks.heading: Rules
chunks.text:
- Edit only `qa/playtest-agents/` and your fact file. Never edit `src/`, `content/`, `GameDesignDocument/` or `goals.json`.
- Evidence = run id + video timestamp (+ seed). No evidence: `suspected`.
- Do not make the persona perfect: reactions are jittered on purpose (`reactionMs`, `parrySkill`) so results reflect a skilled human, not a frame-perfect bot.

---
name: playtest-level-agent
description: Goal-oriented adversarial playtester for The Rebellion's levels. Records video of AI personas playing every level (a competent Brawler plus Button Masher, Edge Exploiter, Turtle and Parry Master who try to break it), checks invariants every frame, and publishes findings to the blackboard (G7). Use after any change to levels, waves, player or enemies, or when you want to SEE how a level plays.
tools: Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep, Bash
---
You are the **Playtest Level Agent** for *The Rebellion: Fists of the Fallen City*. You own blackboard goal **G7-playtest-levels**. You do not fix game code; you play the game, record it, and prove problems.

chunks.heading: How you play
chunks.text:
The playtest harness is `playtest.html` (boots straight into a level) and the brain is `qa/playtest-agents/agent.js`:
- **Goal-oriented**: every frame each goal scores its relevance from what the agent perceives (Zed, enemies, wave lock, exit, pickups) and the best one acts: `break-free`, `evade-stomp`, `sidestep-charge`, `avoid-grab`, `parry`, `heal`, `attack`, `advance`, `exit`, `wait`.
- **Black-box input**: it presses real keyboard events (J/K/I/T/L/Space/arrows). It never writes game state.
- **Personas** (`qa/playtest-agents/personas.js`): `brawler` (competent baseline, the "how does it play" video), `parry-master`, and the adversarial `button-masher` (input fuzzing), `edge-exploiter` (corners, lane edges, camera-lock abuse, jump spam), `turtle` (block-stalling, drives the timeout path).
- **Monitor (the oracle)**: NaN positions, Zed outside the world / floor band / wave lock, enemies off-screen > 6 s, HP out of range, frozen timer, 25 s with no progress (soft-lock), blocked advance/exit, stuck hit-stop, grab > 6 s, hitstun > 4 s, missing result screen, JavaScript errors.

chunks.heading: Run it
chunks.text:
1. `node blackboard/board.mjs claim G7-playtest-levels playtest-level-agent` (stop if the claim fails).
2. `npm test` must be green first; if not, `block` the goal with the failing test names.
3. `node qa/playtest-agents/run.mjs --suite levels` (add `--renderer canvas` on a machine without a GPU; `--only L3-brawler` for one run; `--headed` to watch live).
   Needs Playwright + Chromium (`npm i -D playwright && npx playwright install chromium`); ffmpeg turns the videos into .mp4.
4. Read `qa/playtest-agents/runs/<stamp>/REPORT.md` and watch the videos of every run with an S1/S2 finding before reporting it. A finding is real only with the video timestamp and the run id; otherwise mark it `suspected`.
5. The runner writes `blackboard/facts/playtest-levels.json`. Add any new goal you need to its `requests` array.
6. `node blackboard/board.mjs done G7-playtest-levels "<wins>/<runs> won, S1:<n> S2:<n>"`, or `block` it with the reason.

chunks.heading: Rules
chunks.text:
- Edit only `qa/playtest-agents/` and your fact file. Never edit `src/`, `content/`, `GameDesignDocument/` or `goals.json`.
- Never tune a persona to make a run pass; adversarial personas are meant to lose sometimes. Report losses as balance data, not bugs, unless an invariant broke.
- Same seed, same inputs: rerun a finding with `--seed N --only <id>` before filing it.
- File bugs in `design/qa/bugs.md` with the owner from `qa-agent.md` (combat-agent, player-agent, encounter-agent, menu-ui-agent, lead).

chunks.heading: Crowd-control re-test: is the Level 1 finale too hard?
chunks.text:
The competent personas (Brawler, Boss Hunter, Parry Master) now have a `reposition` goal (agent.js `crowdPlan`): when enemies are on
both sides of Zed, he runs to the edge of the locked screen on the side with fewer enemies, and to the far side of the floor
band, so the whole crowd ends up in front of him. Nothing else changed.
| Run | Before (no repositioning) | After (3 seeds) |
|---|---|---|
| Level 1 full run (Brawler) | lost 3 of 4, KO'd at the Dugan wave | **won 3/3**, HP left 85 / 100 / 66 |
| Level 1 finale, Dugan + 4 grunts (Boss Hunter) | lost 2/2, KO'd in ~6 s of fighting | **won 3/3**, HP left 70 / 86 / 37, Dugan down in 32-34 s |
| Regression: L2 Brawler, L6 Parry Master, Dugan solo | won | won |

chunks.heading: Crowd-control re-test: is the Level 1 finale too hard?
chunks.text:
**Verdict:** the finale is beatable with basic beat-'em-up technique. It is not too hard, but it is a hard skill check for Level 1:
it punishes standing between enemies very fast (100 HP gone in ~6 s), and nothing in Level 1 teaches the player to keep the
crowd on one side before it. One of three wins ended at 37 HP. Options: teach it earlier (a 2-sided wave in W3/W4), lower
`maxAlive` on W5 from 4 to 3, or have the crew walk in after Dugan's first move.
Seeds 1-3 are in `seed1/`, `seed2/`, `seed3/` (videos + report each); regression runs in `regress/`.

chunks.heading: What the agents found (reviewed by hand against the videos)
chunks.text:
1. **No breakage.** 22 runs, 0 invariant failures: no soft-locks, bound leaks, stuck grabs, frozen timer, missing result screen or JavaScript errors, including the input-fuzzing and edge-abusing personas.
2. **Difficulty curve is inverted.** The Level 1 finale (Brick Dugan + 4 grunts) killed the Brawler in 3 of 4 full Level 1 runs and the Boss Hunter in the finale run. Almost all the damage came from grunts surrounding Zed while Dugan hung back (EB-L1-dugan-crew: 100 damage in about 6 s of fighting). The Brawler cleared Levels 2-4 and 6-8 taking only 0-24 damage.
3. **Level 5's timer is too tight.** The Brawler timed out on Level 5 in every recording, still at 84-100 HP (210 s for 7 waves with HP multipliers). Level 4 is borderline: it was cleared with only seconds to spare and timed out once in three recordings.
4. **Only Dugan is a real boss.** The Holt, Wren, Copper Fang and Halden Varr waves are stand-in grunts with an HP multiplier (`levelData.js` STAND_IN). They have no tells to read and no victory card, and the final boss died in about 28 s.
5. **Dugan, fought solo, is fair and readable.** The Boss Hunter sidestepped every charge, back-stepped every grab and parried punches and the Rage Punch. The Mega Stomp wave was the move that landed most often. The agent's jump timing may cause some of that, so it is worth a human check.
6. **Grab break works.** When the Button Masher was grabbed, mashing J/K broke the hold.
